Because `LocalRelease` has no return value, the caller creates a new context regardless and `NewSMContext` overwrites `canonicalRef[supi-pduSessionId]` with the new UUID, so the old context is left in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap`, holding its UE IP and four TEIDs, unreachable by SUPI and PSI.

## Additional Context
A UE that re-requests an existing `pduSessionId` takes this path, and each retry with the same `pduSessionId` repeats it. Each one leaves an SMContext, a `seidSMContextMap` entry, a UE IP and four TEIDs held with no normal path to release them.

This trigger is more common than the other leaks of this pair, which need an NRF or AMF outage. Here a UPF-side problem suffices, and the amplification comes from the UE's own retry behaviour.

UE IP exhaustion arrives well before memory pressure: a `/24` DNN pool holds 254 addresses, and the measured run consumed one per retry from a single UE. Once empty, UPF selection fails for every new session on that DNN.


## How did we find?
We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF holds memory until computer and core is unusable
items.body:
## Describe the bug
When the Core is running (v3.4.3 to v4.0.1) and a UE is connected, if it has a high throughput, the SMF will take memory and never release it. According to a response to my [post on the forum](https://forum.free5gc.org/t/is-there-a-memory-leak-in-the-smf/2690), the SMF should release the memory after the UE is deregistered. The issue here is the SMF will easily use up the systems memory before testing is completed. This causes the machine to stop functioning and requires a manual reboot. 

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
- Free5GC Docker Compose Core is up and running
- With a UE attached and the tunnel interface is up, run `ping <core-ip-address> -i <tun-interface> -A -s 2048`. 
- Monitor the system resources with docker stats

## Expected behavior
The SMF should not be using the entire systems memory.

## Screenshots

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5fd1959a-1bc5-4641-8acd-fbf8e5088c87)

## Environment (please complete the following information):
 - free5GC Version: v3.4.3 - v4.0.1
 - OS:Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04

## Additional context
For now, I've mitigated the issue by using Free5GC v3.3.0.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF: local release leaves a charging session open on the CHF when the PFCP session deletion fails
items.body:
## Bug Description

To set up a PDU session, the SMF opens a charging session on the CHF: `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and remembers the returned charging reference (`smContext.ChargingDataRef`). When such a session is torn down locally — `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease`, e.g. a duplicate PDU session request for the same key — the SMF should close that charging session with `CHARGING_RELEASE`. On the failed-PFCP branch it does not, and it also does not remove the SMContext, so the session is left half-released with its charging session open on the CHF.

The local-release handler releases the PFCP session (`releaseSession`) and switches on the result. `ReleaseChargingSession` (`CHARGING_RELEASE`) is called only on `SessionReleaseSuccess`. On `SessionReleaseFailed` the handler only sets the state back to `Active` and returns — no charging release, and no `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`.

Source analysis on SMF v1.4.3, commit `2232d299`. **Still present on upstream `main` (`1c9d766`, 2026-09-30):** in `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` the `SessionReleaseSuccess` branch still calls `ReleaseChargingSession` (pdu_session.go:1415) while the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch (pdu_session.go:1435) still only reverts the state — no charging release and no `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`. (The `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` handler has the same charging gap on its `SessionReleaseFailed` branch, at 1311/1317; `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` in sm_common.go:7 also still has no charging release. Note: `HandlePDUSessionSMContextUpdate`'s failed branch is *not* a leak — it reverts the context to `Active` and leaves it reachable by `smContextRef`, so a later release can still close it.)

### The charging session is opened at create and its reference stored.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L249-L252

`CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and stores the reference the CHF returns in `smContext.ChargingDataRef`.

### Local release switches on the PFCP result; only success releases charging.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L1340-L1386

```go
pfcpResponseStatus := releaseSession(smContext)
switch pfcpResponseStatus {
case smf_context.SessionReleaseSuccess:
    p.ReleaseChargingSession(smContext)        // :1355-1356  CHARGING_RELEASE to the CHF
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.InActivePending)
    ...
    p.RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext, false)

case smf_context.SessionReleaseFailed:         // :1376-1378  PFCP delete failed / UPF unreachable
    smContext.SetState(smf_context.Active)      // only reverts state
    // <-- no ReleaseChargingSession, no RemoveSMContextFromAllNF
}
```

### The charging release exists only on the success paths.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/charging_trigger.go#L64-L68

`ReleaseChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_RELEASE`. It is reached only from the `SessionReleaseSuccess` branches. The failed-PFCP branch never calls it.

### What makes the PFCP delete fail.

`releaseSession` returns `SessionReleaseFailed` when the UPF does not acknowledge the PFCP session deletion (unreachable UPF, or a rejected/timed-out N4 Session Deletion). The charging session has already been opened at that point, so any such failure leaves it open on the CHF.

## To Reproduce

On SMF v1.4.3, driven through the project's own SMF unit-test harness (`internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session_test.go`): gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP, no real UPF.

**How charging is opened.** The NRF stub lets the SMF discover a CHF, so `CHFSelection` succeeds and `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT`; the CHF stub answers `201` with a charging reference.

**How the PFCP release is made to fail.** The failed-PFCP outcome is reproduced at its exact point with a one-line, env-gated fault in `releaseSession` (`POC_FORCE_RELEASE_FAILED=1` → returns `SessionReleaseFailed`), which is the value a real UPF-unreachable / rejected N4 deletion yields. The leaking code under test (the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch that omits `ReleaseChargingSession`) is unchanged and off by default.

**What is counted.** The CHF stub counts `CHARGING_INIT` (`POST .../chargingdata`) and `CHARGING_RELEASE` (`POST .../chargingdata/{ref}/release`) with `gock.Observe`; SMContext liveness is read with `GetSMContextById(supi, pid)`. The PoC invokes `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` directly on existing contexts, so liveness can still be read with `GetSMContextById`; in the real create path the key is overwritten right after (`NewSMContext`), as described under **The leak** below, which is what makes the stranded context unreachable in production.

```
                 CHARGING_INIT sent | CHARGING_RELEASE sent | live SMContexts | live ChargingDataRef
  control (PFCP OK)              1  |                    1  |              0  |                   0
  LEAK n= 1                      1  |                    0  |              1  |                   1
  LEAK n=10                     10  |                    0  |             10  |                  10
  LEAK n=30                     30  |                    0  |             30  |                  30
```

**The leak.**
- Each of the 30 local releases opened a charging session and then hit `SessionReleaseFailed`.
- Not one `CHARGING_RELEASE` reached the CHF.
- The SMContext is also not removed on this branch, and — crucially — it becomes immediately unreachable **within the same request**: `LocalRelease` is invoked from the create handler for a duplicate key (pdu_session.go:73-75, main 91-93), and the very next line, `NewSMContext` (pdu_session.go:78, main :96), overwrites `canonicalRef` with the new context. On the failed branch the old SMContext is therefore no longer findable by SUPI / PDU Session ID, while it stays held in `smContextPool` and `seidSMContextMap` as a zombie, so no SMF procedure can reach it by SUPI / PDU Session ID. The only remaining path is a UPF association release (`releaseAllResourcesOfUPF`, association.go:163, main :279), which ranges `smContextPool` and may remove the context via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` — but that function sends no `CHARGING_RELEASE`, so the charging session stays open on the CHF either way. If the UPF stays associated (e.g. it rejected the N4 deletion rather than going unreachable), the zombie SMContext itself also persists.
- **Accumulation:** the charging session leaks on the CHF once per failed local release (slope 1), regardless of whether the zombie SMContext is later swept; bounded at 1 only when the exact same session is retried.

## Expected Behavior

The `SessionReleaseFailed` (and default) branch of `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` does **not** call `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, so it must handle cleanup itself: on that branch the SMF should release the charging session (and finish removing the now-unreachable SMContext) before it stops, so a failed PFCP deletion does not leave a charging session open on the CHF together with a zombie SMContext.

(Adding a charging release inside `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF` when `smContext.ChargingDataRef != ""` is a separate, complementary fix — it covers the paths that *do* call `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`, i.e. the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch of the **`HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease`** handler. It does **not** fix this LocalRelease bug on its own, because this branch never reaches that function.)

## Screenshots

N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: SMF v1.4.3 (`2232d299`); reproduced through the SMF unit-test harness, not a full deployment
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64

## Trace Files / Configuration Files

N/A. The PoC runs under `pdu_session_test.go` with gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP; the PFCP failure is produced by the env-gated `POC_FORCE_RELEASE_FAILED` described above.

## PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

## Log File

```
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Send Charging Data Request[Init] successfully
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] In HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease
[TRAC][SMF][CTX] In case SessionReleaseFailed
```
The init is sent; the local release takes the `SessionReleaseFailed` branch; no charging release is logged, and no SMContext removal is logged on this branch.

## System Architecture (Optional)

Single-process Go test harness. NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF are gock HTTP stubs and PFCP is a stub; there is no real UPF and no AMF.

## Additional Context

This is a different bug from the create-time charging leak (e.g. an `ApplySessionRules` failure): there, the full cleanup runs and only the charging release is missing. Here, on `SessionReleaseFailed` the handler does not even run the cleanup — it reverts the state and returns — so both the SMContext and its charging session are left live. The sibling handler `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` (AMF-initiated release) has the same charging gap on its failed branch, but there the SMContext *is* removed, so only the CHF-side charging session is orphaned.

**Anticipated objection.** One might argue that if the PFCP deletion failed the UPF session is still live, so keeping the charging session open is correct. That does not hold here. Because the old SMContext is overwritten in the same create request (above), no SMF procedure can reach it by SUPI / PDU Session ID to retry the release. The one path that can still sweep it is a UPF association release (`releaseAllResourcesOfUPF`), which — in the "UPF unreachable" case — likely runs after a heartbeat failure and removes the context via `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`; but that function sends no `CHARGING_RELEASE`, so **the charging session stays open on the CHF either way**. Only the zombie SMContext is conditional: it is swept if the association drops, and persists if the UPF stays associated (it merely rejected the N4 deletion). The charging leak is unconditional, which is why the failed branch must release charging itself.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] NEF relays the SMF event notification to the AF without type conversion, which may potentially contain SUPI
items.body:
[originally posted as advisory GHSA-g329-33p8-3ggp]

## Description

The NEF's SMF callback forwards the SMF's internal event-notification structure to the AF
**verbatim**, with no conversion and no field redaction. **Two different data types share the name
`EventNotification` — the SMF-facing one defined in 3GPP TS 29.508 and the AF-facing one defined in
TS 29.522 — and the Free5GC-implemented callback sends the former, where the specification requires the latter.**

**Affected file:** `internal/sbi/processor/callback.go` (lines 20–71 and 73–113; serialization at 78),
unchanged on current `main` (`3387eb9`). 

> **NOTE.** CVE-2026-44320 (GHSA-wqfh-gq79-j8mf) reported that the
> `nnef-callback` route group was mounted with **no** authorization middleware, so forged callbacks
> were accepted. **This report concerns what the handler does with a notification that
> has passed that check:** it forwards the SMF's internal event notification to the AF verbatim. Authenticating
> the caller does not redact the payload, and redaction has never been performed on this path.


### Root Cause Analysis

```go
// callback.go:20-23
func (p *Processor) SmfNotification(
    c *gin.Context,
    eeNotif *models.Smf_EvtExpos_NsmfEventExposureNotification,
) {
```

```go
// callback.go:73-86 (excerpt)
func postSmfEventExposureNotificationToAf(
    notifDestination string,
    eeNotif *models.Smf_EvtExpos_NsmfEventExposureNotification,
    requestCtx context.Context,
) error {
    _, reqBody, err := openapi.Serialize(eeNotif, "application/json")
    ...
    httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(requestCtx, http.MethodPost, notifDestination, bytes.NewReader(reqBody))
```

1. The object serialized at `:78` and sent at `:95` is the same `Smf_EvtExpos_*` type the SMF sent in
2. The AF-facing type defined for this purpose is never constructed. `Nef_TrafInfl_EventNotification` in `free5gc/openapi` matches Table 5.4.3.3.4-1 field for field, **The correct target type exists in the codebase — it is simply never constructed**.
3. **Problem:** the callback performs a **pass-through** rather than a **type conversion to 29.522 specified NEF EventNotification type**.

**Two distinct types share the name `EventNotification`, and the callback conflates them.** The SMF-facing type is the one defined in **3GPP TS 29.508 V17.11.0, clause 5.6.2.5**, **Table 5.6.2.5-1: Definition of type EventNotification**. The AF-facing type to be implemented for NEF is the one defined in **3GPP TS 29.522 V17.7.0, clause 5.4.3.3.4, Table 5.4.3.3.4-1: Definition of type EventNotification**. 

The SMF-facing type carries more attributes the AF-facing NEF type. Importantly, among them there are sensitive information such as `supi`, which **TS 33.501 clause 5.9.2.3** names as prohibited from export.


TS 29.522 Table 5.4.3.3.4-1 defines the AF-facing type as exactly fourteen attributes —
`afTransId`, `dnaiChgType`, `sourceTrafficRoute`, `subscribedEvent`, `targetTrafficRoute`,
`sourceDnai`, `targetDnai`, `gpsi`, `srcUeIpv4Addr`, `srcUeIpv6Prefix`, `tgtUeIpv4Addr`,
`tgtUeIpv6Prefix`, `ueMac`, `afAckUri` — and contains **no `supi` attribute at all** unlike the SMF EventNotification defined in TS 29.508. The omission of sensitive information such as
`supi` from the northbound type is the specification's deliberate expression of the boundary, aiming to satisfy the requirement as **TS 33.501 clause 5.9.2.3** specifies:

> -   SUPI shall not be sent outside the 3GPP operator domain by NEF.

**The condition under which supi may leak.** For SMF EventNotification, `supi` is marked `C` (conditional) with no event-specific applicability: it is populated whenever the subscription applies to a group of UE(s) or to any UE, independently of which event fired. 

So a group-scoped or any-UE `UP_PATH_CH` subscription is sufficient. Any spec-compliant SMF that implements Table 5.6.2.5-1 as written can place `supi` in the notification, and the NEF's pass-through will forward it to the AF verbatim.

**Current free5GC behaviour.** We understand that free5GC's own SMF does not populate `supi` today. It builds the
notification at `NFs/smf/internal/context/sm_context.go:765-796` with `event`, `sourceTraRouting`,
`targetTraRouting`, `sourceDnai`, `targetDnai` and `dnaiChgType` only — every one of which has a
counterpart in Table 5.4.3.3.4-1. So in a stock free5GC deployment no SUPI is transmitted today.
However, any future extension to Free5GC's SMF may inadvertently cause this leak.

## Specification

The specification has become progressively more explicit about this, and in the current **19.7.0** release it
is unambiguous. 

**TS 29.522 V19.7.0 clause 4.4.7.4.1** ("Handling of UP path management event
notification" — renumbered from clause 4.4.7.4, where it sits in V17.7.0 through V18.13.0) names
both types in a single requirement:

> If the NEF receives a UP path management event notification from the SMF indicating that the
> subscribed UP path change event has been detected **as defined in 3GPP TS 29.508 [26]**, then the
> NEF shall provide a notification by sending an HTTP POST message that shall include the
> EventNotification data type at least with the subscribed event (e.g. UP Path has changed) to the
> AF identified by the notification destination […]. The NEF may include in the EventNotification
> data type further information **as defined in clause 5.4.3.3.4**.

The **inbound notification is attributed to TS 29.508**; the **outbound data type is bound to clause
5.4.3.3.4 of TS 29.522 itself**. The two emphasized phrases are later additions — the bound-to clause
5.4.3.3.4 appeared in Rel-18, the attribution to TS 29.508 in Rel-19 — but the operative "shall
include the EventNotification data type" is identical in V17.7.0, V17.18.0, V18.13.0 and V19.7.0.
**The NEF is required to emit the TS 29.522 type. free5GC emits the TS 29.508 type.**

Whatever the SMF populates therefore crosses the NEF trust boundary on every normal event, with the
NEF exercising no control over what that is. On any SMF that implements TS 29.508 Table 5.6.2.5-1 as
written, that includes the subscriber's SUPI.

### Impact

Whatever the SMF places in the notification crosses the NEF trust boundary unfiltered, on **every
normal event** rather than only in an error case. The NEF applies no redaction and, being a
pass-through, is structurally incapable of applying any: the boundary TS 33.501 requires it to
enforce is left entirely to whatever the SMF happens to populate.

The exposure is the set of attributes in Table 5.6.2.5-1 with **no** counterpart in Table 5.4.3.3.4-1, which an SMF may populate and the NEF will forward regardless, that may potentially include sensitive information.

The clearest is `supi`, named directly by TS 33.501 clause 5.9.2.3: it is absent from Table
5.4.3.3.4-1 but present in the Go type the NEF serializes (`Smf_EvtExpos_EventNotification.Supi`),
and forwarding it is a direct violation of the security requirement.


### Suggested fix

Construct the NEF's own `EventNotification` (Following TS 29.522 clause 5.4.3.3.4) from the SMF notification,
copying only the fields defined in that schema, and serialize that object instead. Make the
conversion an explicit mapping function with no fall-through, so a field absent from the AF-facing
schema is non-transmissible by construction rather than by inspection.


## Source links

- [`SmfNotification` — takes the SMF type directly](https://github.com/free5gc/nef/blob/f7db48165dfe159be50bca330d5830cc7795f141/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go#L20-L71) — `internal/sbi/processor/callback.go` lines 20–71
- [`postSmfEventExposureNotificationToAf` — verbatim serialize at L78](https://github.com/free5gc/nef/blob/f7db48165dfe159be50bca330d5830cc7795f141/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go#L73-L113) — `internal/sbi/processor/callback.go` lines 73–113

- [SMF builds the notification](https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/dd94a6c4/internal/context/sm_context.go#L765-L796) — `NFs/smf/internal/context/sm_context.go` lines 765–796, at `dd94a6c4`

items.title: [Bugs] UDR: missing return in HandleApplicationDataInfluenceDataSubsToNotifyGet leaks subscriber data (CVE-2026-40245)
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandleApplicationDataInfluenceDataSubsToNotifyGet` in `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go` validates that at least one query parameter (`dnns`, `snssais`, `internal-Group-Id`, `supis`) is present, and sends an HTTP 400 if not. However, the handler does not `return` after `c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, problemDetails)`, so execution continues and the processor is still invoked, returning the full list of Traffic Influence Subscriptions — including SUPIs — in the response body alongside the error.

A second, related trigger exists: when the `snssai` query parameter fails deserialization, the same missing-return pattern applies.

Full technical writeup and CVSS scoring:  https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-wrwh-rpq4-87hf

CVE ID: CVE-2026-40245

## To Reproduce
1. Send a GET request with no query parameters:

```bash
curl -v "http://<udr-host>/nudr-dr/v2/application-data/influenceData/subs-to-notify"
```

2. Observe the response: HTTP status is 400, but the body still contains the full subscription list with subscriber identifiers.

## Expected Behavior
The handler should return HTTP 400 with only the error body, and must not invoke the processor when validation fails.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (confirmed still present; advisory lists affected versions as <= 4.2.1, which appears to understate the range)

## Walkthrough
Root cause: missing `return` statement after two separate `c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, ...)` calls in the same handler. Suggested fix already included in the advisory's Patch section.

## Additional Context
This is an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability — a single unauthenticated GET with no parameters is sufficient. Confirmed still reproducible against the current default branch as of this report.

items.title: [Bugs] UDM: missing SUPI validation in six nudm-sdm handlers leaks internal UDR URL (CVE-2026-42459)
items.body:
## Bug Description
Six GET handlers in `internal/sbi/api_subscriberdatamanagement.go` do not call `validator.IsValidSupi()` before forwarding the `supi` path parameter downstream, unlike `HandleGetAmData` in the same file, which does:

- `HandleGetSmfSelectData` — GET /:supi/smf-select-data
- `HandleGetSupi` — GET /:supi
- `HandleGetTraceData` — GET /:supi/trace-data
- `HandleGetUeContextInSmfData` — GET /:supi/ue-context-in-smf-data
- `HandleGetNssai` — GET /:supi/nssai
- `HandleGetSmData` — GET /:supi/sm-data

A crafted `supi` containing control characters causes UDM to build an invalid internal URL toward UDR, fail Go's `net/url` parsing, and return a 500 that includes the full internal UDR URL (hostname, port, API path structure) in the response body.

This is a missed fix of CVE-2026-27642, which patched the same class of issue only in `internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go`.

Full technical writeup, PoC and CVSS scoring: https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-585v-hcgf-jhfr

CVE ID: CVE-2026-42459

## To Reproduce

```shell
curl "http://<UDM_HOST>/nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-22277%00INJECTED/smf-select-data"
```

Returns HTTP 500 with `detail` containing the full internal UDR URL. For comparison, the protected endpoint:

```shell
curl "http://<UDM_HOST>/nudm-sdm/v2/imsi-22277%00INJECTED/am-data"
```

correctly returns HTTP 400 `"Supi is invalid"`.

## Expected Behavior
All six handlers should validate `supi` with `validator.IsValidSupi()` and return 400 on failure, matching `HandleGetAmData`.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3 (confirmed still present; advisory lists affected versions as <= 4.2.1)

## Walkthrough
Add the same validation block used in `HandleGetAmData` to all six listed handlers:

```go
supi := c.Params.ByName("supi")
if !validator.IsValidSupi(supi) {
    problemDetail := models.ProblemDetails{
        Title:  "Malformed request syntax",
        Status: http.StatusBadRequest,
        Detail: "Supi is invalid",
        Cause:  "MANDATORY_IE_INCORRECT",
    }
    c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, http.StatusText(int(problemDetail.Status)))
    c.JSON(int(problemDetail.Status), problemDetail)
    return
}
```

## Additional Context
Unauthenticated. Discloses internal UDR hostname/port, full internal API path structure, and UDR API version — useful reconnaissance for further attacks against internal 5G core components.

items.title: [Bugs] AMF forwards unsupported reserved SUCI protection scheme IDs to AUSF instead of rejecting early

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Summary

free5gc AMF's `SuciToStringWithError` (`nasConvert/MobileIdentity5GS.go:82`) reads the SUCI protection scheme ID byte (`buf[6]`) and converts it directly to a hex string with no validation against the schemes that free5gc currently supports. When a Registration Request carries a reserved or unsupported scheme ID, the AMF accepts it, allocates a UE context, performs NRF discovery, and forwards the SUCI to the AUSF — only to be rejected by the AUSF after all that work has already been done.

In contrast, open5gs performs this validation early at the AMF level: its `gmm_handle_registration_request` checks that the protection scheme ID is one of the three currently standardized values (0, 1, or 2) and immediately returns `SEMANTICALLY_INCORRECT_MESSAGE` for any other value, avoiding downstream resource consumption.

TS 33.501 Annex C standardizes three protection schemes — Null-scheme (0x0), ECIES Profile A (0x1), and ECIES Profile B (0x2) — while 0x3–0xB are reserved for future standardized schemes and 0xC–0xF are reserved for home-operator proprietary schemes. free5gc currently only implements null-scheme (0). Both implementations currently lack support for ECIES Profile A/B and proprietary schemes, but they differ in how they handle this gap at the AMF layer.

## Environment

- **free5GC Version**: v4.2.2 (git tag), AMF binary built from commit `8b0f444` (2026-04-21), amfconfig Version 1.0.9
- **OS**: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS (Focal Fossa)
- **Kernel version**: 5.4.0-169-generic
- **go version**: go1.25.5 linux/amd64 (AMF binary)

## Affected component

- Component: free5gc AMF (nasConvert library)
- Area: SUCI parsing — `SuciToStringWithError`
- Code path: `nasConvert/MobileIdentity5GS.go:82`, called from `HandleRegistrationRequest` at `handler.go:472`

## Root cause

### free5gc — no scheme ID validation

`SuciToStringWithError` converts the protection scheme byte directly to a string without checking it against the schemes free5gc supports:

```go
// MobileIdentity5GS.go:82
protectionScheme = fmt.Sprintf("%x", buf[6])

if protectionScheme == strconv.Itoa(nasMessage.ProtectionSchemeNullScheme) {
    // null-scheme: parse MSIN
} else {
    // all non-zero values: treat as encrypted scheme output
    schemeOutput = hex.EncodeToString(buf[8:])
}
```

The SUCI is stored as `ue.Suci` and forwarded to the AUSF via `AuthenticationProcedure` → `SendUEAuthenticationAuthenticateRequest`. No check exists anywhere in the call chain.

### open5gs — validates at AMF entry

open5gs checks the scheme ID in `gmm_handle_registration_request` at the same point where other mobile identity validations occur:

```c
if (mobile_identity_suci->protection_scheme_id != OGS_PROTECTION_SCHEME_NULL &&
    mobile_identity_suci->protection_scheme_id != OGS_PROTECTION_SCHEME_PROFILE_A &&
    mobile_identity_suci->protection_scheme_id != OGS_PROTECTION_SCHEME_PROFILE_B) {
    ogs_error("Invalid ProtectionSchemeID(%d) in SUCI",
        mobile_identity_suci->protection_scheme_id);
    return OGS_5GMM_CAUSE_SEMANTICALLY_INCORRECT_MESSAGE;
}
```

This returns an error before any UE context is allocated or any downstream NF is contacted.

### Behavioral difference

| | free5gc | open5gs |
|---|---|---|
| scheme=5 (reserved future) | Accepts → AUSF 403 → Reject | Rejects immediately at AMF |
| scheme=0xF (proprietary) | Accepts → AUSF 403 → Reject | Rejects immediately at AMF |
| Resources consumed before reject | UE context + NRF + AUSF HTTP | None |

## Expected behavior

When the AMF encounters a SUCI protection scheme ID it does not support, it should reject the Registration Request early — before allocating a UE context or contacting downstream NFs.

## Actual behavior

The AMF forwards the SUCI to the AUSF regardless of scheme ID. The AUSF eventually rejects, but only after the AMF has already allocated resources.

## Dynamic verification

A UE was configured with `protectionScheme: 5` (0x5, a reserved future standardized scheme) and sent a Registration Request to an unmodified free5gc AMF:

```text
Handle Registration Request
MobileIdentity5GS: SUCI[suci-0-208-93-0000-5-0-0000000001]   ← scheme=5 accepted
Authentication procedure                                       ← context + NRF + AUSF
Nausf_UEAU Authenticate Request Error: 403, Forbidden          ← AUSF rejects
Send Registration Reject                                        ← only now
```

## Impact

**Low**. This is an input validation / early-rejection hardening issue.

- **Resource waste**: The AMF allocates a UE context and initiates NRF discovery + AUSF HTTP for requests it cannot possibly complete successfully.
- **No authentication bypass**: The AUSF correctly rejects the unsupported scheme.
- **No crash or data leak**: Error handling is correct at both AUSF and AMF layers.
- **open5gs already handles this**: Demonstrates that early rejection at the AMF is a practical and beneficial pattern.

## Suggested fix

Add a scheme ID check in `SuciToStringWithError`:

```go
schemeId, err := strconv.Atoi(protectionScheme)
if err != nil {
    return "", "", fmt.Errorf("invalid protection scheme: %w", err)
}
switch schemeId {
case nasMessage.ProtectionSchemeNullScheme:
    // supported — proceed with null-scheme parsing
default:
    // 0x1–0x2: ECIES Profile A/B — standardized but not yet implemented by free5gc
    // 0x3–0xB: reserved for future standardized schemes
    // 0xC–0xF: reserved for home-operator proprietary schemes
    return "", "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported SUCI protection scheme ID: %d", schemeId)
}
```

If ECIES Profile A/B or proprietary scheme support is added later, extend the switch accordingly.

items.title: [Bugs] PCF: influence-data update notification leaves PCC rules in the SM policy without notifying the SMF when rating-group allocation fails
items.body:
> **Hardening report.** This exit is not reachable in a default deployment: it runs only when `RatingGroupIdGenerator.Allocate()` fails, and that generator's range is `1..math.MaxInt64` (context.go:157). The PoC below shrinks the ID range to make the exit reachable; no handler code is changed.

## Bug Description

When the UDR notifies the PCF of traffic-influence data changes for a PDU session (`POST /npcf-callback/v1/nudr-notify/influence-data/{supi}/{pduSessionId}`), `HandleInfluenceDataUpdateNotify` processes the notifications one by one. It writes directly into the stored SM policy's decision (`decision := smPolicy.PolicyDecision`). For each newly created influence data entry it allocates a rating group for its charging data (notifier.go:107), creates a PCC rule (`util.CreatePccRule`, :156), puts it into the decision and records it in `InfluenceDataToPccRule` (:158). Only after the whole loop does it send the SM policy update notification to the SMF (:170).

If `Allocate()` fails for a later entry, the handler replies with `ERROR_IDGENERATOR` and returns (:113). The PCC rules already created for the earlier entries stay in the SM policy decision, their rating groups stay allocated, and the update notification to the SMF is never sent. So the PCF's SM policy now holds PCC rules that the SMF was never told about, while the UDR receives an error for the notification.

Source analysis on PCF v1.4.3, commit `df6c0daa`. **Still present on upstream `main` (`eb57557`, 2026-08-20):** allocation at notifier.go:110, return at :116, PCC rule creation at :159, and the SMF notification only after the loop.

### The handler writes straight into the stored decision, entry by entry.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go#L63-L66

```go
smPolicy := ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID]
decision := smPolicy.PolicyDecision              // pointer to the stored decision
influenceDataToPccRule := smPolicy.InfluenceDataToPccRule
```

### A failed allocation returns in the middle of the loop.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go#L107-L113

```go
rg, err1 := p.Context().RatingGroupIdGenerator.Allocate()     // :107
if err1 != nil {
    problemDetails := util.GetProblemDetail("rating group allocate error", util.ERROR_IDGENERATOR)
    c.JSON(int(problemDetails.Status), problemDetails)
    return                                                     // :113  earlier PCC rules stay, SMF not notified
}
```

### PCC rules for earlier entries are already in the decision.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go#L152-L171

The PCC rule for each new influence data entry is created and put into the decision (:156-158). The SMF is notified only at :170, after the loop.

## To Reproduce

On PCF v1.4.3, with NRF, UDR and PCF running on loopback (`oauth: false`) and the subscriber's policy data seeded in MongoDB, including one session-level charging entry (`policyData.ues.chargingData`: `dnn` `""`, `filter` `""`, `chargingMethod` `Online`), so each influence data entry gets charging data.

**How allocation is made to fail.** The only source change is an env-gated override of the generator range in `context.go` (`POC_RATING_GROUP_MAX=2`), so the rating-group ID space can be used up in a lab run. The handler code under test is unchanged, and the override is off by default.

**Steps.**
1. Create an SM policy (`pduSessionId` 1). It succeeds (`201`) and uses rating group 1 for its default PCC rule (`PccRuleId-1`).
2. Send one influence-data update notification for that PDU session with two new influence data entries (`poc-n-1`, `poc-n-2`). The first entry gets rating group 2; the second finds the space used up.

**What is counted.** The PCC rules in `GET /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/{supi}-1` before and after the notification, and the SM policy update notifications received by the SMF-side listener (`notificationUri` of the SM policy).

```
                                     HTTP | PCC rules in the SM policy        | SM policy update notifications to SMF
  after create                        201 | [PccRuleId-1]                     | -
  influence notify (2 new entries)  200 (*) | [PccRuleId-1, PccRuleId-2]      | 0

(*) body {"cause":"ERROR_IDGENERATOR"}; ERROR_IDGENERATOR has no entry in PcpErrHttpStatusMap, so the status is 0 and the error goes out as HTTP 200.
```

**The leak.**
- The notification is rejected with `ERROR_IDGENERATOR`, yet the SM policy now holds `PccRuleId-2`, created for the first entry, with rating group 2 still allocated.
- The SMF receives no SM policy update notification, so it never learns about `PccRuleId-2`. The PCF and the SMF now disagree on the SM policy decision.
- The rule and its rating group stay until a later notification for `poc-n-1` changes it, or until the whole SM policy is deleted.

## Expected Behavior

When `HandleInfluenceDataUpdateNotify` fails part-way through the notifications, it should roll back what it already changed in this request: remove the PCC rules it created (and their `InfluenceDataToPccRule` entries) and free the rating groups it allocated, so the stored decision matches what the SMF has. Alternatively, it could build the changes on a copy of the decision and apply them, and notify the SMF, only when the whole notification has been processed.

## Screenshots

N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: PCF v1.4.3 (`df6c0daa`); NRF/UDR/PCF on loopback, not a full deployment
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64

## Trace Files / Configuration Files

PCF configuration with `oauth: false`; the rating-group ID space is shrunk with the env-gated `POC_RATING_GROUP_MAX=2` described above. Notification body:

```json
[
  {"resUri": ".../application-data/influenceData/poc-n-1",
   "trafficInfluData": {"afAppId": "poc-napp-1", "dnn": "internet", "snssai": {"sst": 1, "sd": "010203"},
                        "supi": "<supi>", "trafficRoutes": [{"dnai": "mec"}]}},
  {"resUri": ".../application-data/influenceData/poc-n-2",
   "trafficInfluData": {"afAppId": "poc-napp-2", "dnn": "internet", "snssai": {"sst": 1, "sd": "010203"},
                        "supi": "<supi>", "trafficRoutes": [{"dnai": "mec"}]}}
]
```

## PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

## Log File

```
[INFO][PCF][Callback] [PCF] Handle Influence Data Update Notify
[ERRO][PCF][SMpolicy] rating group allocate error
  -> HTTP 200 {"cause":"ERROR_IDGENERATOR","detail":"rating group allocate error"}
```

No SM policy update notification is sent to the SMF afterwards.

## System Architecture (Optional)

NRF, UDR (with MongoDB) and PCF processes on loopback, plus an HTTP listener standing in for the SMF's notification URI. The influence-data notification is sent directly to the PCF's callback endpoint.

## Additional Context

**Reachability.**   With the default range 1..math.MaxInt64, this exit needs the rating-group space to be exhausted, which does not happen in practice. We still report it because the PCC rules created earlier in the same request are left behind whenever this exit is taken, and it would become reachable if allocation could fail for any other reason.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] PCF: memory leak via CORS middleware registration in setCorsHeader (CVE-2026-41135) — appears already fixed in v4.2.3
items.body:
## Bug Description
`setCorsHeader()`, called by `HTTPOAMGetAmPolicy()` in `pcf/internal/sbi/api_oam.go`, originally called `s.router.Use(cors.New(...))` on every incoming request instead of once at server initialization. Since `router.Use()` in Gin is not idempotent, this permanently grew the router's middleware chain on every request, causing uncontrolled memory growth and eventual OOM/DoS of the PCF.

Full technical writeup, PoC and CVSS scoring: https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-98cp-84m9-q3qp

CVE ID: CVE-2026-41135

## To Reproduce
N/A — see verification note below. Original PoC in the advisory used a request flood against `GET /npcf-oam/v1/am-policy/:supi` while monitoring `docker stats` for unbounded memory growth.

## Expected Behavior
CORS middleware should be registered once at server startup (e.g. in router initialization), not inside a per-request handler.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3

## Walkthrough
On review of the current codebase, this issue appears to be resolved. If confirmed on your side, it would be worth updating the advisory's "Patched versions" field, currently listed as "None", so downstream scanners stop flagging v4.2.3 incorrectly.

## Additional Context
Opening this issue mainly for tracking/closure purposes rather than as an active report.

items.title: [Bugs] SMF Resource Exhaustion via PFCP Session Establishment Failure Handling
items.body:
## Bug Description

A resource exhaustion issue exists in Free5GC v4.2.3 during PFCP Session Establishment failure handling.

During PDU Session establishment, Free5GC uses PFCP signaling over the N4 interface for SMF-UPF communication. If PFCP Session Establishment Responses from the UPF are not received, the SMF continuously retransmits PFCP Session Establishment Requests. However, the resources allocated during the failed session establishment procedure are not properly released.

As a result, repeated failed session establishment attempts can gradually consume UE IP address pool resources. Once the available IP address resources are exhausted, new UEs may fail to establish PDU sessions, causing a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Deploy Free5GC v4.2.3 with a Docker-based 5G Core Network environment.
2. Register multiple UEs and establish normal PDU sessions using UERANSIM.
` docker exec ueransim /ueransim/nr-ue -c /ueransim/config/uecfg.yaml -n 5`
3. Deploy N4Replay between the SMF and UPF as a PFCP interceptor.
    Repository:   https://github.com/hackeryounow/n4repaly/
4. Enable PFCP message interception and drop PFCP Session Establishment Response messages from the UPF.
5. Start a new UE to trigger another PDU Session Establishment procedure.    
`docker exec ueransim /ueransim/nr-ue -c /ueransim/config/uecfg.yaml`
6. Observe that the SMF continuously retransmits PFCP Session Establishment Requests after the responses are dropped.
7. Repeat the procedure multiple times until the available UE IP address pool is exhausted.
8. The continuous PFCP retransmission behavior and resource exhaustion process are shown in the attached animation.

## Expected Behavior

When PFCP Session Establishment fails after retransmission timeout or retry exhaustion, Free5GC should properly release all temporarily allocated resources associated with the failed session establishment procedure.
The SMF should terminate the failed procedure and allow subsequent UEs to establish PDU sessions normally.

## Screenshots

A demonstration video is provided: [https://youtu.be/E1e14Nr_3OA](https://youtu.be/E1e14Nr_3OA)

## Environment

**Please complete the following information:**

- free5GC Version: v4.2.3
- Deployment: Docker-based 5G Core Network
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Desktop
- Kernel version: 138~22.04.1-Ubuntu
- go version: 1.21.8 linux/amd64

## Trace Files

- Configuration Files:
The Free5GC configuration files are provided under `n4repaly/5gc/free5gc/` in the attached archive.
The UE IP address pool network prefix was modified to `/29` to facilitate reproduction of the resource exhaustion behavior.
- PCAP File:
  `multi-est-pfcp-session-free5gc.pcapng` contains the PFCP signaling traces between SMF and UPF.
- Log File:
  `smf.log` contains the SMF log output during the reproduction.


## System Architecture (Optional)
The test environment consists of: 
- 5G Core Network: Free5GC v4.2.3
- UE simulator: UERANSIM
- PFCP test component: [N4Replay](https://github.com/hackeryounow/n4repaly)
- Interface under test: N4 interface between SMF and UPF
Architecture:
```
UERANSIM
   |
   |
Free5GC AMF/SMF -------- N4Replay -------- UPF
                              |
                              |
                    PFCP message interception
                    and response dropping
```
Deployment environment:
- Containerized deployment using Docker
- SMF and UPF communicate through PFCP over the N4 interface
## Additional Context

- Vulnerability Type:  Resource Exhaustion（Denial of Service）
- CVSS v4：`CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:H`

items.title: [Bugs] AUSF authentication contexts for the same SUPI can be overwritten by concurrent requests
items.body:
## Bug Decription

The AUSF stores per-subscriber authentication state in a global `sync.Map` (`UePool`) keyed **only by SUPI**. Every successful
`POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications` that receives auth data from UDM creates a new `AusfUeContext` and stores it under that SUPI key
unconditionally, with no check for an authentication already in progress and no per-session unique identifier (CWE-362).

`internal/context/context.go`:
```go
func AddAusfUeContextToPool(ausfUeContext *AusfUeContext) {
    ausfContext.UePool.Store(ausfUeContext.Supi, ausfUeContext) // overwrites
}
```
`internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go` (per request):
```go
ausfUeContext := ausf_context.NewAusfUeContext(ueid)
ausfUeContext.AuthStatus = models.AusfUeAuthenticationAuthResult_ONGOING
ausf_context.AddAusfUeContextToPool(ausfUeContext)
```

Concurrent accepted EAP-AKA' authentication requests for the same SUPI each get a distinct `EapID` generated locally in the AUSF. When UDM returns fresh or otherwise different authentication vectors, the associated `K_aut` / `XRES` / `RAND` are also different. However, all requests collapse onto one context key and the same EAP context URL (`/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications/{suci}/eap-session`). Only the last write survives; earlier contexts are orphaned.

When the EAP response for an earlier challenge arrives, the AUSF looks up the context by SUPI and validates AT_MAC against the **overwritten** `K_aut`, failing with `EAP-AKA' integrity check fail`. An attacker with access to the AUSF SBI/N12 interface who keeps a flood of authentication requests for a target SUPI can deny that subscriber's authentication for the duration of the flood.

`sync.Map` makes the individual map operations safe; the root issue is the **session design** (SUPI as the sole key + unconditional `Store`), not a missing mutex.

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce:
1. Change config: standard `ausfcfg.yaml` with OAuth2 disabled in the observed lab/default profile. NRF + UDM (or a UDM stub) so authentication vectors are returned.
2. Code patch: none required for the AUSF. (Our harness used a counter-based UDM stub returning a `LEGIT` vector on the first request and a different `ATTACK` vector afterwards to make the downstream authentication failure deterministic;
   the AUSF overwrite defect itself is independent of the stub. See `pocs/mock_udm_race.py`.)
3. Run command — Phase 1 (overwrite): send N concurrent `POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications` for the same SUCI, e.g. `suci-0-001-01-0-0-0-0000000002` (`pocs/dos_poc.py`). Observed: 24/24 HTTP 201, 24 distinct EapIDs, a single context URL, and 24 `Add SuciSupiPair (...) to map.` log lines for the same SUPI within ~4 ms.
4. Run command — Phase 2 (effect on a valid response) (`pocs/poc_race_eap.py`):
   - Baseline: one auth + a valid EAP-AKA' response computed with `K_aut` of that challenge → `Correct RES value, EAP-AKA' auth succeed` (HTTP 200, EAP success).
   - Race: one auth, then a flood of ~20 concurrent auths for the same SUCI, then submit the original valid EAP response → `EAP-AKA' failure: EAP-AKA' integrity check fail` (HTTP 200, EAP notification failure).
5. Dump packet: captured in
   `evidence/20260617-155129-live-repro-pcap/issue2-sbi.pcap` with `sudo tcpdump -i lo -w /tmp/issue2-sbi.pcap 'tcp port 8000 or tcp port 8100 or tcp port 8200'` while running the baseline and flood phases.

## Expected Behavior

Concurrent authentication procedures for the same SUPI must not corrupt each other. Either:
- generate a unique per-session identifier, store the context under it, and return it in the auth context URL; or
- allow only one in-progress authentication per SUPI via an atomic check-and-insert and reject the rest with `409 Conflict` (`AUTHENTICATION_IN_PROGRESS`).

A valid EAP response for an in-progress challenge should be verified against that challenge's own context.

## Screenshots

N/A (log excerpts under Trace Files).

## Environment

 - free5GC Version: AUSF built from `main` @ commit `bfc4a10094dbacbd862baa4686829f3fcc06ce1e` (module pseudo-version `v0.0.0-20260522003208-bfc4a10094db`); also present in `ausf` v1.4.4
 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS
 - Kernel version: 5.15.0-179-generic
 - go version: go1.26.3 linux/amd64
 - C compiler version (optional): N/A (pure-Go network function)

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files
No configuration change is required. The lab used a standard `ausfcfg.yaml`.
Sanitized lab configs are included under `config/ausfcfg.yaml` and `config/nrfcfg.yaml`.
Relevant observed runtime values:
- OAuth2 disabled (`OAuth2 setting receive from NRF: false`).
- AUSF listening on `0.0.0.0:8100` (`Start SBI server (listen on 0.0.0.0:8100)`).

### PCAP File
`evidence/20260617-155129-live-repro-pcap/issue2-sbi.pcap` — loopback capture (SBI ports 8000/8100/8200) of a baseline run followed by the flood run. The flood is visible as ~20 short client connections to the AUSF (`:8100`) within ~15 ms during the `POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications` flood window, plus the long-lived AUSF↔UDM h2c connection. SBI is HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c), so request paths are HPACK-compressed in the bytes; the connection burst correlates 1:1 with the AUSF log overwrites, which remain the decisive evidence.

### Log File
- `logs/REDACTED-baseline-success.txt` — baseline EAP-AKA' success.
- `logs/REDACTED-flood-failure.txt` — flood overwrites + `integrity check fail`.
- `logs/mock-udm-counters.txt` — UDM stub LEGIT/ATTACK counters.
Raw batches under `evidence/phase1-context-overwrite/` and `evidence/phase2-auth-failure/`. A fresh live reproduction with raw PoC stdout,
full AUSF/NRF/UDM logs and the PCAP is under `evidence/20260617-155129-live-repro-pcap/` (baseline `auth succeed` at 12:34:02Z; flood → 21 overwrites + `integrity check fail` at 12:34:36Z).

[mock-udm-counters.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29089442/mock-udm-counters.txt)
[REDACTED-flood-failure.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29089441/REDACTED-flood-failure.txt)

## System Architecture (Optional)

Bare-VM lab (VirtualBox). NRF + AUSF + UDM (stub). Attacker = any client able to reach the AUSF SBI endpoint (internal SBA network in a real deployment).

<!-- Failed to upload "ausfcfg.yaml" -->

<!-- Failed to upload "nrfcfg.yaml" -->

## Walkthrough (Optional)

Starting from an observation that many concurrent auths for one SUCI yield distinct EapIDs but a single context URL, we traced the AUSF context pool. `AddAusfUeContextToPool` stores by SUPI and overwrites unconditionally; the EAP confirmation handler re-reads by SUPI. We reproduced the overwrite (Phase 1) and the resulting authentication failure for a valid earlier response (Phase 2).
Note: Phase 2 used a synthetic but protocol-valid EAP-AKA' client and a UDM stub to make the overwrite observable; we did not run a full UERANSIM/AMF registration trace.

## Additional Context

Suggested fix (per-session id):
```go
sessionID := uuid.New().String()
ausfUeContext := ausf_context.NewAusfUeContext(sessionID)
ausfUeContext.Supi = ueid
ausf_context.AddAusfUeContextToPool(ausfUeContext)
// URL: /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications/{sessionID}/eap-session
```

Additional hardening: per-SUPI rate limiting; enforce OAuth2/mTLS on SBI.

- CWE: CWE-362 (concurrent execution with improper synchronization / shared key).
- Suggested CVSS for triage: `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` → 7.5 High
- Prior art: distinct from CVE-2026-33063 (AUSF nil-pointer DoS) and CVE-2026-44318 (BSF concurrent-map panic). No CVE found for this AUSF
  context-overwrite issue. free5gc/ausf#62 mentions `UePool` growth/no delete functions, but does not cover concurrent auth context overwrite or  authentication failure for an earlier valid EAP response.
- This issue is being filed because maintainers asked us to move the private advisory into GitHub Issues. Full PoC scripts and raw evidence can be provided privately if preferred.

items.title: [Bugs] PCF: SM policy create leaves the SM policy behind when rating-group allocation for the default PCC rule fails
items.body:
> **Hardening report.** This exit is not reachable in a default deployment: it runs only when `RatingGroupIdGenerator.Allocate()` fails, and that generator's range is `1..math.MaxInt64` (context.go:157). The PoC below shrinks the ID range to make the exit reachable; no handler code is changed.

## Bug Description

When the SMF creates an SM policy (`POST /sm-policies`), `HandleCreateSmPolicyRequest` first stores a new SM policy in the UE context (`NewUeSmPolicyData` → `ue.SmPolicyData[smPolicyID]`, smpolicy.go:116). While building the policy decision it allocates a rating group from `RatingGroupIdGenerator` for the session-level charging data of the default PCC rule (:214).

If that `Allocate()` fails, the handler replies with `ERROR_IDGENERATOR` and returns (:220). It does not remove the SM policy stored at :116. The SMF does not get a `201` with a `Location`, so it never sends `POST /sm-policies/{smPolicyId}/delete`, which is the only path that removes it (`HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest`). At this exit the default PCC rule is not yet in the decision, and the decision is attached to the SM policy only later (:368), so what is left behind is the SM policy itself.

Source analysis on PCF v1.4.3, commit `df6c0daa`. **Still present on upstream `main` (`eb57557`, 2026-08-20)**, at the same line numbers (:116, :214, :220).

### The SM policy is stored first.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go#L112-L116

### The rating-group allocation fails and the exit removes nothing.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go#L214-L220

```go
rg, err1 := p.Context().RatingGroupIdGenerator.Allocate()      // :214
if err1 != nil {
    logger.SmPolicyLog.Error("rating group allocate error")
    problemDetails := util.GetProblemDetail("rating group allocate error", util.ERROR_IDGENERATOR)
    c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, problemDetails.Cause)
    c.JSON(int(problemDetails.Status), problemDetails)
    return                                                      // :220  SM policy stays in ue.SmPolicyData
}
```

### Only the SMF's delete removes it.

https://github.com/free5gc/pcf/blob/df6c0daacbc7fe5f610f19665e169f013eb05721/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go#L516-L582

`HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest` removes the SM policy (`delete(ue.SmPolicyData, smPolicyId)`, :555) and frees its rating groups (`FreeID`, :572; `delete(ue.RatingGroupData, …)`, :582). It is reached only when the SMF deletes an SM policy it was told was created (`201` + `Location`).

## To Reproduce

On PCF v1.4.3, with NRF, UDR and PCF running on loopback (`oauth: false`) and the subscriber's policy data seeded in MongoDB. Stored SM policies are read back through the PCF's own `GET /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/{smPolicyId}`.

**How allocation is made to fail.** The only source change is an env-gated override of the generator range in `context.go` (`POC_RATING_GROUP_MAX=N` → `idgenerator.NewGenerator(1, N)`), so the rating-group ID space can be used up in a lab run. The handler code under test is unchanged, and the override is off by default. The PCF is started fresh for the run.

**What is seeded.** For one SUPI: the session-level charging data for the UE (so the handler allocates a rating group for the default PCC rule). `POC_RATING_GROUP_MAX=1`.

**Steps.** A first create (`pduSessionId` 1) takes the only rating group and stays live, as an existing session would. Every following create, each with a new `pduSessionId`, then hits the exit. The PoC uses one SUPI with `pduSessionId`s beyond 15 to show the slope; the PCF does not validate the range. With a real SMF (ids 1-15) the count is bounded at 15 per UE and grows with the number of UEs.

**What is counted.** For each failed create: whether `GET` on its `smPolicyID` still answers `200`, and the PCC rules (`policy.pccRules`) it still holds.

```
                               create HTTP | SM policies still stored | PCC rules still stored
  holder (pduSessionId 1)              201 |                        1 | [PccRuleId-1]
  failed creates n= 1             200 (*)  |                        1 | 0
  failed creates n=10             200 (*)  |                       10 | 0
  failed creates n=30             200 (*)  |                       30 | 0
  control: delete holder 204, next create 201 (the rating group is freed and reused)

(*) body {"cause":"ERROR_IDGENERATOR"}; see Additional Context.
```

**The leak.**
- Every failed create leaves its SM policy in `ue.SmPolicyData` (30 creates → 30 SM policies, slope 1).
- The SMF never receives a `Location`, so it never deletes them.
- **Control:** deleting the live SM policy frees its rating group, and the next create succeeds. The generator itself works; only the error exit leaks.

## Expected Behavior

Any error exit of `HandleCreateSmPolicyRequest` after :116 should undo what the request already did: remove the SM policy from `ue.SmPolicyData` and free the rating groups allocated in this request, as `HandleDeleteSmPolicyContextRequest` does. A single deferred cleanup that is skipped on success would cover this exit together with the other error exits of the handler.

## Screenshots

N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: PCF v1.4.3 (`df6c0daa`); NRF/UDR/PCF on loopback, not a full deployment
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64

## Trace Files / Configuration Files

PCF configuration with `oauth: false`; the rating-group ID space is shrunk with the env-gated `POC_RATING_GROUP_MAX` described above. Seeded documents (one SUPI, S-NSSAI `01010203`, DNN `internet`):

```
policyData.ues.chargingData  {ueId, snssai, dnn: "", filter: "", chargingMethod: "Online"}          # session level
```

## PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

## Log File

```
[INFO][PCF][SMpolicy] Handle CreateSmPolicy
[ERRO][PCF][SMpolicy] rating group allocate error
  -> HTTP 200 {"cause":"ERROR_IDGENERATOR","detail":"rating group allocate error"}
[INFO][PCF][SMpolicy] Handle GetSmPolicyContext
  -> HTTP 200 (the SM policy from the failed create is still stored)
```

## System Architecture (Optional)

NRF, UDR (with MongoDB) and PCF processes on loopback; the SM policy requests are sent directly to the PCF. No SMF or AMF.

## Additional Context

**Reachability.** With the default range `1..math.MaxInt64`, this exit needs the rating-group space to be exhausted, which does not happen in practice. We still report it because the SM policy is left behind whenever this exit is taken, and it becomes reachable as soon as the ID space is made smaller or allocation can fail for another reason.

**Persistence.** Nothing else removes the leftover SM policy: the SMF never learns its id, and the PCF has no eviction, timeout or sweep over `ue.SmPolicyData`. It is replaced only when a later create arrives with the same `supi-pduSessionId` (smpolicy.go:112-114), so in practice it is bounded at one per PDU session id (at most 15) per UE, and grows with the number of UEs.

**Error status.** `ERROR_IDGENERATOR` has no entry in `PcpErrHttpStatusMap` (pcf_util.go), so `GetProblemDetail` returns `Status: 0` and the error is sent with HTTP `200` (still the case on `main`). The SMF therefore receives a `200` with a problem-details body for a failed create.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.

items.title: [Bugs] UDM: subscriptionId accepted without validation, leaks internal error on oversized/crafted input (GHSA-f72w-jgfw-hhm9)
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandleUnsubscribeForSharedData`, `HandleModifyForSharedData`, and `HandleUnsubscribe` in `internal/sbi/api_subscriberdatamanagement.go` extract `subscriptionId` from the path and pass it straight to the processor with no format/length validation — unlike `supi`/`ueId` in the same file, validated via `validator.IsValidSupi()`/`IsValidGpsi()`. Oversized or special-character values propagate deep enough to trigger an unhandled internal error that leaks implementation details.

Full technical writeup, PoC and CVSS scoring: GHSA-f72w-jgfw-hhm9
https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-f72w-jgfw-hhm9

Status: accepted by maintainers, CVE requested (not yet assigned).

## To Reproduce
```shell
curl -v -X DELETE "http://<UDM_IP>:80/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions/$(python3 -c 'print("A"*10000)')"
# 500, {"detail":"unsupported scheme[]", "cause":"SYSTEM_FAILURE"}

curl -v -X DELETE 'http://<UDM_IP>:80/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions/%24ne'
# 500, same detail

curl -v -X PATCH "http://<UDM_IP>:80/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions/%7B%22%24ne%22%3Anull%7D" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}'
# 404, {"title":"User not found","cause":"USER_NOT_FOUND"} — reaches business logic instead of being rejected at input validation
```

## Expected Behavior
`subscriptionId` should be validated (e.g. UUID or the format used at generation time) immediately after extraction, returning 400 with a generic message on failure — mirroring the existing `supi`/`ueId` pattern.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3

## Walkthrough
Add a validation check for `subscriptionId` before calling the processor, following the pattern already used for `supi`/`ueId` in `HandleGetAmData`/`HandleUnsubscribe`. Avoid propagating `err.Error()` verbatim to the client.

## Additional Context
The `500 "unsupported scheme[]"` suggests the value is later passed to something expecting a well-formed URI (e.g. `url.Parse`) without the caller anticipating arbitrary input at that stage.

items.title: [Bugs] UDM: verbose deserialization errors expose internal Go struct names (GHSA-999x-p7pg-f5hm)
items.body:
## Bug Description
`HandleSubscribeToSharedData`, `HandleSubscribe`, `HandleModify`, and `HandleModifyForSharedData` in `internal/sbi/api_subscriberdatamanagement.go` return the raw Go `error.Error()` string directly in the `Detail` field of the `ProblemDetails` response on deserialization failure, exposing fully-qualified internal Go struct names. Same underlying pattern as the AMF advisory (GHSA-xw5p-5pgh-4xq5), reported separately as a distinct codebase.

Full technical writeup, PoC and CVSS scoring: GHSA-999x-p7pg-f5hm
https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-999x-p7pg-f5hm

Status: accepted by maintainers, CVE requested (not yet assigned).

## To Reproduce
```shell
curl -v -X POST http://<UDM_IP>/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '[1,2,3]'
# 400, "detail":"[Request Body] json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type models.SdmSubscription"

curl -v -X PATCH http://<UDM_IP>/nudm-sdm/v2/shared-data-subscriptions/sub123 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '[1,2,3]'
# 400, "detail":"...models.SdmSubsModification"
```

Truncated JSON on the same endpoint instead returns a generic, non-disclosing "unexpected end of JSON input" — the leak is specific to type-mismatch errors.

## Expected Behavior
Client-facing `Detail` should be generic; full error detail should stay server-side only.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3

## Walkthrough
```go
err = openapi.Deserialize(&sharedDataSubsReq, requestBody, "application/json")
if err != nil {
	logger.SdmLog.Errorln("[Request Body] " + err.Error()) // logs only
	rsp := models.ProblemDetails{
		Title:  "Malformed request syntax",
		Status: http.StatusBadRequest,
		Detail: "The request body is malformed or does not match the expected schema.",
	}
	c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, http.StatusText(int(rsp.Status)))
	c.JSON(int(rsp.Status), rsp)
	return
}
```
A shared helper across all four affected handlers is recommended.

## Additional Context
Defense-in-depth / reconnaissance-hardening issue; no direct exploitation demonstrated.

items.body:
## Bug Description
Multiple handlers in `internal/sbi/api_communication.go` (`HTTPAMFStatusChangeSubscribeModify`, `HTTPCreateUEContext`, `HTTPEBIAssignment`, `HTTPRegistrationStatusUpdate`, `HTTPReleaseUEContext`, `HTTPUEContextTransfer`, `HTTPN1N2MessageTransfer`, `HTTPN1N2MessageSubscribe`, `HTTPAMFStatusChangeSubscribe`) return the raw Go `error.Error()` string directly in the `Detail` field of the `ProblemDetails` response on deserialization failure, exposing fully-qualified internal Go struct names.

Full technical writeup, PoC and CVSS scoring: GHSA-xw5p-5pgh-4xq5
https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/security/advisories/GHSA-xw5p-5pgh-4xq5

Status: accepted by maintainers, CVE requested (not yet assigned).

## To Reproduce
```shell
curl -v -X POST http://<AMF_IP>/namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/imsi-222771234567890/assign-ebi \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '[1,2,3]'
```

Response: `400`, `"detail":"[Request Body] json: cannot unmarshal array into Go value of type models.AssignEbiData"` — discloses the internal struct name from a simple type-mismatch (array instead of object). Truncated JSON / empty body instead produce a generic "unexpected end of JSON input" that does not leak struct names.

## Expected Behavior
Client-facing `Detail` should be a generic message; the full error should only go to server-side logs (which already happens via `logger.CommLog.Errorln`).

## Environment
- free5GC Version: v4.2.3

## Walkthrough
```go
err = openapi.Deserialize(&assignEbiData, requestBody, applicationjson)
if err != nil {
	logger.CommLog.Errorln(reqbody + err.Error()) // full detail stays in logs
	rsp := models.ProblemDetails{
		Title:  "Malformed request syntax",
		Status: http.StatusBadRequest,
		Detail: "The request body is malformed or does not match the expected schema.",
	}
	c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, http.StatusText(http.StatusBadRequest))
	c.JSON(http.StatusBadRequest, rsp)
	return
}
```
A shared helper across all nine affected handlers is recommended for consistency.

## Additional Context
Defense-in-depth / reconnaissance-hardening issue — SBI is expected to be protected by mTLS/OAuth2, but this aids an attacker with SBI access in constructing precisely-typed payloads. Same underlying pattern also reported for UDM (GHSA-999x-p7pg-f5hm).

items.title: [Bugs] SMF does not release the CHF charging session when PDU session create fails at ApplySessionRules
items.body:
## Bug Description

To set up a PDU session, the SMF opens a charging session on the CHF: `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and remembers the returned charging reference (`smContext.ChargingDataRef`). If the session setup then fails, the SMF should close that charging session again with `CHARGING_RELEASE`. The setup failure path does not do that.

Right after opening the charging session, the create applies the PCF's session rules (`ApplySessionRules`). If that fails, the handler calls `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`, which runs the SMF's cleanup, `RemoveSMContextFromAllNF`. That cleanup terminates the SM policy on the PCF, unsubscribes from the UDM and removes the SMContext. It has no charging release at all. `ReleaseChargingSession` (`CHARGING_RELEASE`) is only called from the normal PDU session release handlers.

So the SMF rejects the session, cleans up everything else, and leaves the charging session open on the CHF. It has also just deleted the SMContext that held the only copy of `ChargingDataRef`, so nothing in the SMF can ever close it later. Every such failed setup leaves one more open charging session on the CHF.

### The create opens the charging session first.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L249-L252

`HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate` selects a CHF and calls `CreateChargingSession` (`:252`). `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT` and stores the reference the CHF returns in `smContext.ChargingDataRef`.

```go
if err = p.Consumer().CHFSelection(smContext); err != nil {
	logger.PduSessLog.Errorln("chf selection error:", err)
} else {
	p.CreateChargingSession(smContext)                                   // :252  CHARGING_INIT to the CHF
}
```

### The next step can fail, and its failure exit goes to the cleanup.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go#L255-L262

`ApplySessionRules` (`:256`) installs the session rules from the PCF's SM policy decision. It returns an error when the context ends up with no session rule (`sm_context_policy.go:44-46`). The handler then calls `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext` and returns.

```go
if err = smContext.ApplySessionRules(smPolicyDecision); err != nil {    // :256
	smContext.Log.Errorf("PDUSessionSMContextCreate err: %v", err)
	p.makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext(c, smContext,
		nasMessage.Cause5GSMRequestRejectedUnspecified,
		&smf_errors.SubscriptionDenied)                                  // -> RemoveSMContextFromAllNF
	return
}
```

### The cleanup releases the SM policy, but not the charging session.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/sm_common.go#L7-L49

`RemoveSMContextFromAllNF()` terminates the SM policy on the PCF when `smContext.SMPolicyID != ""` (`:17`), unsubscribes from the UDM, and then removes the SMContext (`:49`). There is no `ReleaseChargingSession` call in it, and nothing checks `smContext.ChargingDataRef`.

```go
func (p *Processor) RemoveSMContextFromAllNF(smContext *smf_context.SMContext, sendNotification bool) {
	smContext.SetState(smf_context.InActive)
	// ...
	if smContext.SMPolicyID != "" {
		if err := p.Consumer().SendSMPolicyAssociationTermination(smContext); err != nil {   // :17  SM policy DELETE to the PCF
			smContext.Log.Errorf("SM Policy Termination failed: %s", err)
		} else {
			smContext.SMPolicyID = ""
		}
	}
	// ... UDM unsubscribe ...
	// <-- no ReleaseChargingSession / CHARGING_RELEASE
	go p.sendSMContextStatusNotificationAndRemoveSMContext(smContext, sendNotification)       // -> RemoveSMContext(ref) at :49
}
```

### The charging release exists, but only on the normal release paths.

https://github.com/free5gc/smf/blob/2232d2992f204207e58830ac8ee55bf0cd832f92/internal/sbi/processor/charging_trigger.go#L64-L68

`ReleaseChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_RELEASE`. It is called from `HandlePDUSessionSMContextRelease` and `HandlePDUSessionSMContextLocalRelease` on `SessionReleaseSuccess`. The create failure path never calls it.

```go
func (p *Processor) ReleaseChargingSession(smContext *smf_context.SMContext) {
	// ...
	p.Consumer().SendConvergedChargingRequest(smContext, smf_context.CHARGING_RELEASE, multipleUnitUsage)
```

**What makes the create fail here.** `ApplySessionRules` fails whenever the SM policy decision from the PCF leaves the context with no session rule. The charging session has already been opened at that point, so any such failure leaves it open.

## To Reproduce

On SMF v1.4.3, driven through the project's own SMF unit-test harness (`internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session_test.go`): gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP, no real UPF. **No change to the SMF source.** The only harness change is the PFCP listen address.

**How charging is opened.** The NRF stub lets the SMF discover a CHF, so `CHFSelection` succeeds and `CreateChargingSession` sends `CHARGING_INIT`. The CHF stub answers with `201` and a charging reference.

**How the create is made to fail.** The PCF stub answers `POST /sm-policies` with `201` and an SM policy decision whose `sessRules` is empty. `ApplySessionRules` then returns `"ApplySessionRules: no session rule"`, and the handler takes the `:256` failure exit into `makeEstRejectResAndReleaseSMContext`. This is the natural failure path, with no injection.

**What is sent.** 30 `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts`, one per UE: 30 distinct SUPIs, each with PDU Session ID 10.

**What is counted.** The stubs count requests with `gock.Observe`:
- `CHARGING_INIT` reaching the CHF (`POST .../chargingdata`)
- `CHARGING_RELEASE` reaching the CHF (`POST .../chargingdata/{ref}/release`)
- SM policy terminations reaching the PCF (`POST .../sm-policies/{id}/delete`)

The SM policy terminations show that the cleanup actually ran. On the SMF, the test also checks the SMContext pool with `GetSMContextById(supi, pduSessionId)`.

```
                       HTTP | CHARGING_INIT sent | CHARGING_RELEASE sent | SM policy terminations sent
  after 1 UE            403 |                  1 |                     0 |                           1
  after 10 UEs          403 |                 10 |                     0 |                          10
  after 30 UEs          403 |                 30 |                     0 |                          30

total: 30 UEs, 30 charging sessions opened on the CHF, 0 released; 30 SM policies terminated, 30 SMContexts removed
```

**The leak.**
- All 30 creates open a charging session on the CHF and then fail at `ApplySessionRules`.
- The cleanup runs every time. The PCF receives all 30 SM policy terminations, and all 30 SMContexts are removed from the SMF pool (0 left at the end).
- But not one `CHARGING_RELEASE` reaches the CHF.
- The cleanup that runs on this path simply has no charging release, so each failed create leaves one open charging session on the CHF.

**The accumulation.** The count of open charging sessions rises by exactly one per failed create. The SMContext that held `ChargingDataRef` has been removed, so the SMF has no record left to release it with, and no later procedure in the SMF revisits it. The open sessions stay on the CHF until the CHF expires them by its own means.

## Expected Behavior

When a PDU session create fails after CHARGING_INIT has been sent to the CHF, the SMF should send CHARGING_RELEASE for that charging session before discarding the SMContext, so that no charging session is left open on the CHF.

## Screenshots

N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: SMF v1.4.3 (`2232d299`); reproduced through the SMF unit-test harness, not a full deployment
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS
- Kernel version: 6.8.0-139-generic
- go version: go1.25.5 linux/amd64
- C compiler version (optional):

## Trace Files

### Configuration Files

N/A. The PoC runs under the project's `pdu_session_test.go` harness with gock-stubbed NRF/UDM/PCF/CHF and a stub PFCP; reproduction conditions are described above.

### PCAP File

N/A. This is a code-logic issue, unrelated to the packet level.

### Log File

One failed create:

```
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] CHF Selection for SMContext SUPI[imsi-208930000030000] PDUSessionID[10]
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Handle SendConvergedChargingRequest
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Send Charging Data Request[Init] successfully
[ERRO][SMF][PduSess][pdu_session_id:10][supi:imsi-208930000030000] PDUSessionSMContextCreate err: ApplySessionRules: no session rule
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] UE[imsi-208930000030000] PDUSessionID[10] Release IP[10.60.0.1]
[INFO][SMF][PduSess][pdu_session_id:10][supi:imsi-208930000030000] smContext[urn:uuid:ecb02e76-f93d-4f7f-b114-f87fb377ecd9] is deleted from pool
```

The init is sent and the SMContext is deleted from the pool, but no charging release is logged. Over the whole run, `ApplySessionRules: no session rule` and `is deleted from pool` each appear 30 times.

## System Architecture (Optional)

## Walkthrough (Optional)


## Additional Context

Every create that opens a charging session and then fails at `ApplySessionRules` leaves one open charging session on the CHF. The SMF has already sent a reject, so neither the AMF nor the UE will ever release this session. The SMF itself has deleted the SMContext and with it `ChargingDataRef`, so it cannot release it either.

This is a different bug from the SM policy leak on the async reject path. There, the whole cleanup is skipped. Here, the cleanup runs to completion and only the charging release is missing from it, so the SM policy is terminated correctly while the charging session is not.

## How did we find?

We found this bug by using our (work-in-progress) static analysis tool, manually verified it, and made a runnable PoC.
